title: Maze Path Finder
spec: A grid of integers is provided where zero is open space and one is a wall. The function `navigate(grid)` must find a path from the top left corner to the bottom right corner using a breadth first search. Track visited coordinates to avoid infinite loops and backtracking. If a valid path is found, return a list of coordinate tuples representing the steps taken. If no path exists, return an empty list.

title: Poker Hand Evaluator
spec: Accept a list of five tuples where each tuple has a rank string and a suit string. The function `evaluate(cards)` must determine the highest poker hand achieved. Check for a flush by matching suits and a straight by verifying consecutive ranks after converting face cards to numerical values. Output the result as a plain string, such as flush, straight, pair, or high card.

title: Markdown to HTML Parser
spec: Accept a list of raw text lines. The function `parse(document)` should convert lines starting with a hash symbol into header tags, and lines starting with a dash into list item tags inside an unordered list. Wrap all other non-empty lines in paragraph tags, and ignore empty lines entirely. Track the state of active lists to close them properly when the list ends. Return a single joined string representing the full document.

title: Regional Sales Aggregator
spec: Accept a list of tuples containing a region string, a product string, and an amount integer. The function `aggregate(records)` should group the total amounts by region and product, skipping any records where the amount is negative. Calculate the percentage of total sales each product represents within its specific region. Return a list of tuples containing the region, product, total amount, and percentage rounded to two decimal places.

title: Dependency Task Scheduler
spec: Accept a list of pairs where the first task string must be completed before the second task string. The function `schedule(dependencies)` must perform a topological sort using depth first search to find a valid execution order. Keep track of visited nodes to detect dependency cycles. Return a list of tasks in a safe execution order, or an empty list if a circular dependency makes scheduling impossible.

title: Hierarchical Log Filter
spec: Accept a list of strings formatted with a date, time, severity, and message separated by brackets. The function `filter(logs, level)` must parse each line manually without external libraries. Return a list of messages that match the specified severity level or higher, assuming a strict hierarchy of debug, info, warning, error, and critical. Discard any improperly formatted lines during parsing.

title: Sudoku Board Validator
spec: Accept a list of nine lists, each containing nine integers from zero to nine, where zero represents an empty cell. The function `validate(board)` must return a boolean indicating if the grid is valid according to standard rules. Use sets to verify that no non-zero number repeats in any horizontal row, vertical column, or three by three subgrid block. The logic should short circuit and return false upon finding the first violation.

title: Reverse Polish Notation Calculator
spec: Accept a string containing numbers and basic arithmetic operators separated by spaces. The function `calculate(expression)` should evaluate the string as reverse polish notation using a stack mechanism. Pop elements when operators are encountered, perform the math, and push the result back. Return the final integer result, but return a zero if a division by zero occurs or if the expression is malformed and leaves extra items on the stack.

title: Time Interval Merger
spec: Accept a list of tuples representing start and end times as integers. The function `merge(intervals)` must sort them by start time and combine any overlapping or touching intervals into continuous blocks. Determine the total covered time across all consolidated intervals, and identify the single longest gap of continuous unused time between any two consecutive intervals. Return a tuple of the total time and the maximum gap time.

title: Connect Four Winner Check
spec: Accept a list of six lists, each with seven strings representing a game board where cells contain either red, yellow, or an empty string. The function `check(grid)` must scan all horizontal, vertical, and diagonal directions for four consecutive matching pieces. Ensure that bounds checking is handled correctly when searching diagonals. Return the winning color as a string, or an empty string if there is no winner.

title: Vending Machine Change Manager
spec: Accept a list of tuples representing inserted coin amounts and item prices, alongside a list of available machine coins. The function `dispense(transactions, coins)` should process each transaction and attempt to calculate exact change using a greedy algorithm based on the available coins. If exact change is impossible, skip the transaction and leave the coin pool unchanged. Return a tuple of the successful transaction count and the remaining list of machine coins.

title: Run Length Compression
spec: Provide a module with logic to compress and expand text. The entry function `process(text, compress)` accepts a string and a boolean flag. If the flag is true, compress sequences of identical letters into the letter followed by its count, such as transforming three consecutive letters of the same type into the character followed by the number three. If the flag is false, reverse this process to expand the letter and count pairs back into the original text. Return the resulting transformed string.

title: Ten Pin Bowling Scorer
spec: Accept a list of integers representing pins knocked down in each roll of a standard ten pin game. The function `score(rolls)` must calculate the total score by iterating through ten frames. Add appropriate bonus points for strikes and spares by looking ahead at subsequent rolls. Handle the complex logic for the tenth frame where extra rolls are awarded. Return the final calculated integer score.

title: DNA Sequence Translator
spec: Search a long sequence string of nucleotides for a specific start codon. The function `translate(sequence)` must then read the sequence in groups of three characters, mapping them to amino acids using a small provided set of rules. Stop translation immediately if a stop codon is encountered. Handle potential frame shifts by verifying the sequence length. Return a list of all complete translated amino acid strings found.

title: Directory Tree Measurement
spec: Accept a nested structure of tuples where a file is a string name and an integer size, and a folder is a string name and a list of child nodes. The function `measure(node)` should recursively traverse the structure to calculate the total size of all nested files. Track the largest file encountered during the traversal. Return a tuple containing the total combined size and the string name of the largest single file.

title: Grid Robot Navigation
spec: Simulate a robot moving on a grid. The function `simulate(commands, start, obstacles)` accepts a list of directional commands, a starting coordinate tuple, and a list of obstacle coordinate tuples. Track the facing direction and update coordinates for forward movements. If a movement would land on an obstacle, ignore that step but continue processing the rest of the commands. Return a tuple of the final coordinates and the total number of obstacle collisions.

title: Batch Password Validator
spec: Check a list of passwords against multiple security criteria. The function `verify(passwords)` must ensure each password has a minimum length of eight, and contains an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit, and a punctuation mark. Verify that no password contains repeated sequential substrings of three or more characters. Return a list of strings containing only the passwords that successfully pass all validation checks.

title: Roman Numeral Equation Evaluator
spec: Accept a string containing an equation written entirely in roman numerals, separated by a plus symbol and an equals sign. The function `evaluate(equation)` must parse the three distinct numeral groups into integers by iterating over their characters and handling subtraction cases like four or nine. Perform the addition of the first two numbers and determine if the result equals the third number. Return a boolean representing whether the equation is correct.

title: Binary Search Tree Analyzer
spec: Determine if a binary tree is a valid search tree, calculate its maximum depth, and count the total number of leaf nodes. The function `analyze(tree)` accepts a nested tuple structure representing nodes, where each tuple contains an integer value, a left child, and a right child. Recursively verify that left children are smaller and right children are larger than their parents. Return a tuple containing the boolean validity, the maximum integer depth, and the integer leaf count.

title: Matrix Multiplication and Transpose
spec: Accept two nested lists representing mathematical matrices. The function `multiply(first, second)` must first verify that they can be multiplied by checking if the column count of the first matches the row count of the second. If they can, compute the standard dot product matrix using nested loops. Transpose the resulting matrix by swapping its rows and columns. Return the final two dimensional list, or an empty list if the initial dimension check fails.

title: Filtered Anagram Grouper
spec: Accept a list of strings and organize them into collections of anagrams. The function `group(words)` should sort the characters of each string to find common root words and group them into lists. Filter out any anagram groups that contain fewer than three words. Sort the remaining groups by the character length of the words they contain in descending order. Return the sorted list of grouped lists.

title: Sentence Palindrome Extractor
spec: Accept a long string containing multiple sentences separated by periods. The function `extract(text)` should split the text, and within each sentence, ignore all spaces and punctuation while converting everything to lowercase. Locate the longest continuous palindromic substring within that cleaned sentence using an expansion outward from centers approach. Return a list of tuples containing the original parsed sentence and its longest found palindrome.

title: Elevator Route Simulator
spec: Simulate an elevator system handling a series of passenger requests. The function `operate(requests, floors)` accepts a list of tuples representing the origin floor and destination floor for each passenger, alongside an integer for the maximum floor. Track the current floor of the elevator, moving it sequentially to pick up and drop off passengers. Keep track of the doors opening and closing, and calculate the total distance moved. Return the total number of floors traveled.

title: INI Configuration Parser
spec: Accept a list of strings representing a configuration file. The function `configure(lines)` should parse lines starting with a bracket as section headers, and lines with an equals sign as key and value pairs. Ignore comments starting with a semicolon and skip completely empty lines. Construct and return a list of tuples, where each tuple contains a section name, a key, and its corresponding value, maintaining the order they appeared in the file.

title: Shortest Path Graph Search
spec: Accept a graph represented as a list of tuples containing two node names and an integer distance. The function `search(edges, start, end)` must find the shortest path from the start node to the end node using an algorithm like Dijkstra. Maintain a priority queue of distances and a set of visited nodes to traverse the graph efficiently. Return a tuple containing the minimum total distance and a list of node names representing the optimal path taken.

title: Music Playlist Duration Aggregator
spec: Write a function `calculate(playlist)` that computes the total duration of a series of songs. The input is a string of comma separated entries where each contains an artist, a dash, a title, and the duration in parenthesis. Group the total time by artist by parsing the minutes and seconds for each track. Handle the overflow of seconds into minutes and hours properly. Return a list of tuples containing the artist name and their total formatted time as a string, sorted alphabetically by artist. Example: an input with two songs by the same artist lasting three minutes and thirty seconds each returns a total time of seven minutes and zero seconds.

title: Game of Life Simulator
spec: Create a function `simulate(grid, steps)` that computes the state of a cellular automaton after a given number of iterations. The input is a two dimensional list of integers where one is alive and zero is dead. In each step, a live cell with fewer than two or more than three live neighbors dies, while a dead cell with exactly three live neighbors becomes alive. The grid edges are not wrap around. Return a new two dimensional list representing the final grid state. Example: a grid of zeros with a horizontal line of three ones becomes a vertical line of three ones after one step.

title: Minesweeper Board Annotator
spec: Write a function `annotate(board)` that takes a two dimensional list of characters representing a minesweeper grid. Mines are marked with an asterisk and empty spaces with a dash. Replace all dashes with the count of mines in their immediate eight adjacent neighbors. If a dash has no neighboring mines, replace it with a zero. Keep the asterisks exactly where they are. Return the fully annotated two dimensional list of strings. Example: a board with one mine and one empty space returns an asterisk and a one.

title: Nested Expression Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(expression)` that parses and calculates the result of a mathematical string. The string contains integers, addition, subtraction, multiplication, and nested parentheses, with arbitrary whitespace. Evaluate the operations following standard mathematical precedence, where parentheses have the highest priority, followed by multiplication, and then addition and subtraction from left to right. Return the final integer result. Example: "2 + 3 * ( 4 - 1 )" outputs eleven.

title: Tic Tac Toe State Checker
spec: Implement a function `check(board)` that receives a three by three list of strings containing the letters X, O, or a space. Determine the current state of the game based on standard rules. If there is a line of three identical letters horizontally, vertically, or diagonally, return the letter of the winner. If both players have winning lines, return the word Invalid. If there is no winner but the board is completely filled, return the word Draw. If the board is incomplete and no one has won, return the word Ongoing. Example: a complete diagonal of X returns the letter X.

title: Balanced Tag Verifier
spec: Create a function `verify(document)` that checks if a string containing custom tags is perfectly balanced. A starting tag consists of a word inside angle brackets, and an ending tag has a slash before the word. Parse the string sequentially to track opened tags. When a closing tag is found, it must match the most recently opened unclosed tag. If any tags are unmatched, nested incorrectly, or left unclosed at the end, return false. Otherwise, return true. Example: "" returns true.

title: Battleship Fleet Validator
spec: Write a function `validate(grid)` that checks if a ten by ten grid contains a valid battleship fleet. The grid is a list of lists of integers where one is a ship part and zero is water. A valid fleet consists of exactly one four cell ship, two three cell ships, three two cell ships, and four one cell ships. Ships can be placed horizontally or vertically but must be straight lines. Ships must not touch each other, not even diagonally. Return a boolean indicating whether the fleet is valid. Example: an empty grid returns false.

title: Boggle Grid Word Finder
spec: Write a function `search(grid, words)` that takes a four by four list of single uppercase letters and a list of target words. A word is valid if it can be formed by sequentially connecting adjacent cells horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. The same cell cannot be used more than once per word. Return a sorted list of all words from the target list that can be successfully traced in the grid. Example: finding the word CAT in a grid where the letters C, A, and T are adjacent.

title: Multi Area Flood Fill
spec: Implement a function `fill(matrix)` that identifies and measures all enclosed areas of zeros in a grid of integers. The input is a two dimensional list where ones represent walls and zeros represent empty space. Find all distinct contiguous regions of zeros, where contiguous means connected horizontally or vertically. Return a list of integers representing the size of each distinct region, sorted in descending order. Example: a grid with two entirely separate regions of size two and three outputs [3, 2].

title: Subtitle Synchronization Shifter
spec: Write a function `shift(subtitles, offset)` that adjusts the timestamps in a list of subtitle entries. Each entry is a plain string formatted as a sequence number, followed by a start and end time in hours, minutes, seconds, and milliseconds separated by a colon, and then the text. Add the given integer offset in milliseconds to both times. Handle all rollovers for seconds, minutes, and hours accurately, assuming standard time bounds. Return a list of completely updated subtitle strings. Example: adding a thousand milliseconds shifts all times forward by one second.

title: Text Paragraph Word Wrapper
spec: Create a function `wrap(text, width)` that takes a single long string and an integer line width. Break the text into multiple lines such that no line exceeds the width, breaking only at spaces. If a single word is longer than the width, it must be put on its own line and allowed to overflow. Remove any trailing spaces from each line. Return a list of strings representing the formatted lines. Example: wrapping the words hello world with width five yields a list of two strings.

title: License Key Grouping
spec: Write a function `format(key, size)` that reformats a string of alphanumeric characters and dashes. First, strip the input string of all dashes and convert it to uppercase. Insert new dashes such that every group of characters has exactly the given size, except possibly the first group which can be shorter but must contain at least one character. Next, calculate a checksum by summing the alphabetical index of every letter where A is one, ignoring digits. Take the sum modulo twenty six, convert it to a letter, and append it to the very end after a dash. Return the newly formatted string. Example: an input with a single letter A yields a checksum of A appended at the end.

title: Common Free Time Finder
spec: Implement a function `find(schedules, duration)` that calculates the earliest available time block for a group of people. The input is a list of schedules, where each schedule is a list of busy intervals represented as tuples of integers denoting minutes from midnight. Find the earliest continuous block of free time of at least the given duration that works for everyone. Return a tuple of start and end times for this block, or an empty tuple if no common time exists. Example: finding thirty free minutes among overlapping busy blocks yields the first available half hour.

title: Full Paragraph Justification
spec: Create a function `justify(words, limit)` that takes a list of words and an integer line width, returning a list of fully justified text lines. Pack as many words as possible into each line without exceeding the limit. Distribute extra spaces evenly between words. If spaces cannot be divided evenly, place the extra spaces in the leftmost gaps. The last line of the text should be left aligned with a single space between words and padded with spaces on the right. Example: justifying a list of four words to a width of sixteen characters.

title: Pascal Triangle Path Sum
spec: Write a function `generate(rows, target)` that builds Pascal's triangle up to the given number of rows. The first row has a single one, and each subsequent row is formed by summing adjacent elements of the previous row. Once built, search for the target integer within the triangle. If found, calculate the sum of all numbers in the shortest path from the top of the triangle down to that specific number, moving only to adjacent elements in the row below. If the target appears multiple times, use the one highest up. Return the sum as an integer, or zero if not found. Example: finding the number three returns a path sum of five.

title: Domino Chain Sequence Finder
spec: Create a function `chain(dominoes)` that determines if a given list of domino tiles can be arranged in a continuous line. Each domino is a tuple of two integers. They can be rotated, meaning the numbers in a tuple can be flipped. The second number of a tile must perfectly match the first number of the next tile in the sequence. Return a valid ordered list of tuples if a complete chain is possible using all tiles, or an empty list if it is not. Example: three connecting dominoes return the ordered sequence.

title: ISBN Format Verification
spec: Write a function `verify(code)` that checks whether a given string is a valid ten or thirteen digit book number. Ignore all hyphens in the input. For a ten digit number, multiply each digit by a descending weight from ten to one, and the total sum must be a multiple of eleven. The final character of a ten digit code can be the uppercase letter X to represent ten. For a thirteen digit number, alternate the weights between one and three, and the total sum must be a multiple of ten. Return a boolean indicating validity. Example: a valid ten digit book number returns true.

title: Text Log Frequency Counter
spec: Implement a function `count(logs)` that parses a list of plain string log lines. Each line contains a date, a time, an event level like error or warning, and a message, all separated by spaces. Aggregate the data to tally the number of times each event level occurs per unique date. Return a list of tuples, where each tuple contains the date string and a list of frequencies for error, warning, and info levels in that exact order. Sort the outer list chronologically by date. Example: a list with two errors on the same day returns the day and the counts two, zero, and zero.

title: Sliding Window Maximum Finder
spec: Create a function `maximize(numbers, size)` that computes the maximum value in every contiguous sublist of the given size within an array of integers. As a window of the given size moves from the far left of the array to the far right, record the largest integer visible in the window at each step. Return a list of these maximum values in order. If the array is empty or the window size is zero, return an empty list. Example: an array of numbers from one to five with a window of three yields three maximum values.

title: Spiral Matrix Extractor
spec: Write a function `extract(matrix)` that takes a two dimensional list of integers and returns a single list of all its elements in spiral order. Start at the top left corner and proceed right across the first row, then down the last column. Continue by moving left across the bottom row, and then up the first column. Repeat this inward spiraling pattern until all elements have been visited exactly once. Handle non square matrices gracefully. Example: a three by three grid of numbers from one to nine yields a spiraled list of all nine integers.

title: Hexadecimal Color Gradient Interpolator
spec: Create a function `interpolate(start, end, steps)` that generates a gradient of colors between two hexadecimal strings. Each input string is a hash symbol followed by six hex digits representing red, green, and blue components. Calculate the intermediate colors by linearly interpolating each color component separately over the given number of steps, rounding to the nearest integer. Ensure the first and last colors in the output match the start and end inputs. Return a list of formatted hexadecimal strings representing the full gradient sequence. Example: interpolating black to white in three steps returns black, gray, and white hex codes.

title: Software Version Comparator
spec: Create a function `compare(versions)` that sorts a list of software version strings in ascending order. Each version string consists of integers separated by dots, optionally ending with a dash and the word alpha or beta. Compare the integers from left to right, treating missing parts as zeros. If a version includes an alpha or beta tag, it is considered strictly older than the exact same version without a tag, and alpha comes before beta. Return the newly sorted list of version strings. Example: version one point zero dash alpha comes before version one point zero.

title: Deck Shuffler and Dealer
spec: Implement a function `deal(players, cards)` that simulates handing out cards to a number of players. The input deck is a list of plain strings representing cards. Before dealing, perform a cut on the deck by moving the top half of the cards to the bottom. If the deck has an odd number of cards, the extra card goes to the bottom half. Distribute the cards one by one to each player in order, wrapping around until the required number of cards per player is met. Return a list of lists containing each player's hand, or an empty list if the deck runs out prematurely. Example: dealing two cards to two players returns two hands of two cards.

title: Simple Key Value Parser
spec: Write a function `parse(text)` that processes a string containing comma separated key and value pairs. Each pair is separated by a colon. Keys and values may have leading or trailing whitespace which must be trimmed. If a value is wrapped in square brackets, treat it as a list of strings split by spaces. Ignore any pairs that are completely empty. Return a list of tuples containing the cleaned key and its corresponding string or list value. Example: a string with name bob and colors red and blue returns a tuple for name and a tuple with a list for colors.

title: Morse Code Message Decoder
spec: Create a function `decode(message)` that converts a string of morse code dots and dashes back into english text. Each letter is separated by a single space, and each word is separated by three spaces. First, split the sequence into words, and then split each word into characters. Map each sequence of dots and dashes to its corresponding uppercase letter using standard morse rules. If any word contains an invalid sequence, replace that specific word entirely with the word ERROR in the output. Return the fully decoded string with single spaces between words. Example: a valid sequence outputs the words HI THERE.

title: Ranked Choice Voting Evaluator
spec: Determine the winner of an election using ranked choice voting logic by calling `elect(ballots)`. Take a list where each element is a list of candidate names representing a single voter preference order. Count the top choices for all voters. If no candidate has a strict majority of top votes, remove the candidate with the fewest top votes from all ballots entirely. Repeat this process until one candidate secures a majority, and return that candidate name. If a tie occurs at the bottom, remove all tied candidates. Example: given [['a', 'b'], ['c', 'a'], ['a', 'c']], return 'a'.

title: E-commerce Cart Checkout
spec: Calculate the final price of an online shopping cart using `checkout(items, coupons)`. Process a list of tuples containing item price, weight, and category name. Calculate the initial subtotal. Apply the single best valid discount from a list of coupons, which can be either a flat amount off the total or a percentage off a specific category. Finally, add a shipping fee based on the total weight, charging five dollars for every pound over ten pounds. Return the final calculated price as a float.

title: Darts Match Scorer
spec: Simulate a turn based darts game starting at five hundred and one points by calling `score(throws)`. Process a list of string multipliers like single, double, or triple, and integer base values, reducing the total score accordingly. If a throw drops the score below zero, or exactly to one, the current turn is a bust and the score resets to what it was at the start of that round of three throws. Return the final remaining score after all throws in the list are processed.

title: Train Ticket Fare Calculator
spec: Calculate the daily travel cost for a commuter using `fare(trips)`. Evaluate a list of trips, where each trip provides a starting station zone integer, an ending station zone integer, and an hour of travel. Charge a base rate of two dollars plus an additional fifty cents for every zone boundary crossed. Apply a one dollar peak time surcharge for trips occurring between seven and nine in the morning. Ensure the total charge for the day never exceeds a fixed daily cap of twenty dollars, returning the final computed cost.

title: Bill Splitting Balancer
spec: Compute the net balances for a group of friends sharing costs by calling `settle(expenses)`. The input is a list of tuples detailing the person who paid, the total amount, and a list of people who share the expense equally. Calculate the net positive or negative balance for each person. Return a list of tuples specifying who needs to pay whom and the exact amount to clear all debts, ensuring the number of transactions is kept to a minimum.

title: Levenshtein Edit Distance
spec: Calculate the minimum number of single character edits required to change one string into another using `distance(source, target)`. The allowed operations are insertion, deletion, or substitution of a character. Build a matrix to evaluate the cost of each operation at every character position iteratively. Return the integer value found at the bottom right of the matrix representing the total edit distance. Example: transforming kitten to sitting returns three.

title: Simple CPU Emulator
spec: Simulate a simple processor executing operations on four registers by implementing `execute(instructions)`. Handle string commands to load a constant into a register, add two registers, multiply two registers, and jump to a different instruction index if a specified register holds a zero. Continue execution until the instruction pointer moves past the end of the list. Return a list of the final integer values held in the four registers.

title: English Noun Pluralizer
spec: Convert a list of singular English nouns into their plural forms based on standard rules using `pluralize(words)`. Check if the word ends in s, x, z, ch, or sh to append es. If it ends in a consonant followed by y, replace the y with ies. Check against a small list of irregular words where child becomes children and mouse becomes mice. For all other words, simply append an s, and return the newly transformed list of words.

title: Calendar Month Grid Generator
spec: Generate a visual grid representation of a month using `calendar(year, month)`. First, determine the day of the week for the first day using an established mathematical algorithm. Handle leap years properly to assign twenty nine days to February when applicable. Construct and return a list of weeks, where each week is a list of seven integers, using zero to represent empty days before the start and after the end of the month.

title: Tennis Match Scorer
spec: Compute the score of a tennis game from a sequence of point winners using `referee(points)`. Translate the point counts into standard tennis terminology like love, fifteen, thirty, and forty. If both players reach three points, set the state to deuce, and track advantage states until one player wins by two clear points. Return a string representing the current score or the name of the winning player if the game is complete.

title: Inventory Bin Packer
spec: Allocate a list of item weights into the minimum number of containers using `pack(items, capacity)`. Sort the items in descending order of their weights first. Iterate through the items, placing each into the first container that has enough remaining capacity space, opening a brand new container if none of the existing ones can fit it. Return a list of containers, where each container is a list of the specific weights it currently holds.

title: User Role Permission Resolver
spec: Determine the effective access rights for a user based on role assignments by calling `permissions(assignments, hierarchy)`. The assignments input maps users to direct roles, and the hierarchy input maps roles to lists of permissions and parent roles. Recursively traverse the hierarchy to gather all inherited permissions for a user. Return a list of unique permission strings granted to the specified user, ensuring no infinite loops occur if roles somehow have circular references.

title: Infix to Postfix Converter
spec: Transform a mathematical expression from infix notation to postfix notation by implementing `convert(expression)`. Iterate over a list of string tokens including numbers, operators, and parentheses. Push operators onto a stack based on strict precedence rules, and append numbers directly to the output. Pop operators off the stack when encountering closing parentheses or lower precedence operators. Return the final arranged sequence of tokens as a list.

title: Simple JSON Stringifier
spec: Convert nested python lists, strings, integers, and boolean values into a raw formatted string representation using `stringify(data)`. Iterate recursively through the data structures. Ensure strings are wrapped in double quotes and inner quotes are escaped with backslashes. Represent boolean values as lower case strings true or false, and separate list items with commas. Return the final fully concatenated string.

title: Tetris Line Clearer
spec: Process a matrix of integers representing a playing board by calling `clear(grid)`. Ones represent filled blocks and zeroes represent empty space. Identify any horizontal rows that contain only ones. Remove these full rows entirely, shift all remaining rows down by the amount cleared, and insert new rows of zeroes at the top to maintain the original height. Return a tuple containing the modified grid and the integer count of rows removed.

title: Wordle Guess Evaluator
spec: Compare a five letter guess against a secret word to generate game feedback using `evaluate(guess, secret)`. First, identify letters in the exact correct position and mark them as green. Then, for remaining letters, check if they exist elsewhere in the secret word and mark them as yellow, but only up to the number of times that letter actually appears in the secret word. Mark all other letters as gray, returning a list of the five color strings.

title: CIDR Subnet Calculator
spec: Calculate network boundaries given an internet protocol version four address string and an integer prefix length by implementing `subnet(address, prefix)`. Convert the four octets into a thirty two bit integer. Apply a bitwise mask derived from the prefix to find the base network address. Calculate the broadcast address by setting the remaining host bits to one. Return a tuple containing the network address string, the broadcast string, and the total usable host count.

title: Recipe Ingredient Scaler
spec: Adjust the quantities in a list of ingredients by a given multiplier using `scale(ingredients, factor)`. Each ingredient is a tuple of name, amount, and a unit string. If the scaled amount in ounces exceeds sixteen, convert it to pounds. If teaspoons exceed three, convert to tablespoons. Return a new list of tuples with the updated amounts rounded to two decimal places and the appropriate adjusted unit strings.

title: Bank Account Ledger
spec: Maintain a running bank balance by processing a list of transaction tuples using `process(transactions)`. Each tuple contains an action type string and an amount. Add amounts for deposits and subtract for withdrawals. Apply a flat five percent penalty if a withdrawal drops the balance below zero. If an action is labeled as interest, increase the current positive balance by that percentage. Return the final float balance and an integer count of penalties applied.

title: Glob Pattern Matcher
spec: Determine if a text string matches a given search pattern by calling `match(pattern, filename)`. The pattern can contain normal letters, a question mark that matches exactly one of any character, or an asterisk that matches zero or more of any character. Use a backtracking approach or dynamic programming to evaluate the wildcard possibilities. Return a boolean indicating whether the entire filename string is fully consumed by the pattern.

title: Traffic Light Simulator
spec: Model cars passing through a single intersection controlled by a traffic light using `simulate(arrivals, ticks)`. The arrivals input is a list of integers representing the number of cars arriving at each time step. The light alternates between green for five steps and red for five steps. During a green light, up to three waiting cars can pass through per step. Track the growing queue during red lights. Return the total number of cars that successfully passed within the given ticks.

title: Flight Connection Router
spec: Find the quickest path between two cities by implementing `route(flights, start, destination)`. Evaluate a list of flight tuples containing origin, destination, departure hour, and arrival hour. Ensure that connections have at least one hour of layover time but no more than six hours. Traverse the available options and calculate the total duration from the first departure to the final arrival. Return a list of airport names representing the fastest valid sequence.

title: Cryptographic Playfair Cipher
spec: Encrypt a string using a five by five letter grid by calling `encrypt(message, keyword)`. Generate the grid from the keyword, filling the rest with unused alphabet letters and treating i and j as the same letter. Split the message into pairs of letters, inserting a dummy letter if a pair has matching characters. For each pair, apply the cipher rules based on whether they share a row, a column, or form a rectangle in the grid. Return the final encrypted string.

title: Pagination Link Generator
spec: Create a sequence of page numbers for a navigation component using `paginate(current, total)`. The function must return a list of integers and string ellipses. Always include page one, the final total page, the current page, and one page immediately before and after the current page. Replace any gap of missing numbers between these required pages with an ellipsis string. Example: given current four and total ten, return one, ellipsis, three, four, five, ellipsis, ten.

title: Log Window Anomaly Detector
spec: Identify bursts of high activity in a sequence of integer log timestamps by calling `detect(timestamps, threshold)`. Slide a fixed time window of three hundred seconds across the timeline, checking every unique timestamp as a starting point. Count how many events fall within that five minute window. If the count strictly exceeds the given threshold integer, record the start time. Return a sorted list of all unique window start times that triggered the anomaly.

title: Arithmetic Expression Tokenizer
spec: Create a function `evaluate(expression)` that takes a mathematical string containing numbers, parenthesis, plus, and minus signs, and evaluates it. It should parse through the characters one by one. Skip any space characters. If a digit is found, gather all contiguous digits into an integer. If parentheses are found, process the expression inside them recursively or use a stack to keep track of current signs and results. The function returns the final evaluated integer. For example, passing the string containing two plus open parenthesis three minus one close parenthesis returns four.

title: Network Packet Demultiplexer
spec: Write a function `demultiplex(stream)` that processes a list of raw network packets where each packet is a tuple containing a port number, a sequence number, and a string payload. Group the packets by port number. For each port, sort the packets by their sequence numbers. Concatenate the payloads in order to form a complete message for each port. Skip any packets that have an empty payload or a negative sequence number. Return a list of tuples, each containing a port number and its reconstructed message string, sorted by port number in ascending order.

title: Conference Schedule Conflict Detector
spec: Create a function `check(sessions)` that takes a list of conference sessions, where each session is a tuple with a room name, a start time in minutes, and an end time in minutes. Group the sessions by room name. For each room, sort the sessions by start time. Check if any session overlaps with the next one in the same room; an overlap occurs if a session starts strictly before the previous one ends. If any room has overlapping sessions, return the name of the first room found with a conflict when sorted alphabetically. If no rooms have conflicts, return the string none.

title: Grocery Store Inventory Tracker
spec: Write a function `audit(transactions)` that computes the current stock for various grocery items based on a sequence of daily transactions. Each transaction is a tuple of item name, transaction type which is either incoming or outgoing, and an integer quantity. Maintain a current count for each item starting at zero. Process each transaction by adding or subtracting the quantity. If an outgoing transaction requests more than the available stock, skip that entire transaction and record the item name as short. Return a tuple containing a list of final stock counts formatted as tuples of item name and quantity sorted alphabetically, followed by a list of unique item names that experienced a shortage sorted alphabetically.

title: Hotel Room Booking Allocator
spec: Create a function `allocate(requests)` that assigns hotel rooms to incoming guest requests. The input is a list of guest requests where each request is a tuple of guest name, preferred floor number, and requested room type which is either single or double. The hotel has exactly three floors, numbered one to three, and each floor has exactly ten single rooms and ten double rooms. For each request, try to assign a room on the preferred floor of the requested type. If the preferred floor is full for that type, try the other floors starting from floor one. If no rooms of the requested type are available anywhere, assign nothing to that guest. Return a list of tuples containing guest name, assigned floor, and room type, in the order the requests were processed.

title: Cinema Seating Assigner
spec: Write a function `seat(groups)` that assigns adjacent seats to groups of people in a single cinema row of twenty seats. The input is a list of integers representing group sizes. The seats are numbered one to twenty and are initially empty. For each group, find the first contiguous block of empty seats from the left that fits the entire group. If such a block is found, mark those seats as occupied and record the starting seat number for this group. If no single block is large enough, the group is turned away and receives a starting seat of zero. Return a list of starting seat numbers corresponding to each group in the input order.

title: Book Index Generator
spec: Create a function `index(pages)` that builds a back of book index from a list of pages. Each page is a tuple of page number and a list of words found on that page. Process each page by examining its words. Ignore words that have fewer than four letters. For all other words, convert them to lowercase and record the page numbers where they appear. Ensure that if a word appears multiple times on the same page, the page number is only recorded once per word. Return a list of tuples where each tuple contains a word and a sorted list of page numbers, with the overall list sorted alphabetically by word.

title: Factory Shift Worker Roster
spec: Write a function `roster(shifts)` that determines total hours worked by factory employees over a week. The input is a list of shift records, each being a tuple of worker name, day of week, start hour in military time, and end hour in military time. For each shift, calculate the duration by subtracting start from end. If the end hour is smaller than the start hour, assume the shift crossed midnight and add twenty four to the end hour before subtracting. Sum the total hours for each worker. Return a list of tuples containing the worker name and total hours, sorted by total hours in descending order, and then alphabetically by name for ties.

title: Restaurant Menu Allergen Filter
spec: Create a function `filter(menu)` that identifies safe dishes for a customer with specific allergies. The input menu is a list of tuples, each containing a dish name and a list of ingredient strings. The customer is allergic to peanuts, dairy, and shellfish. Process each dish and check its ingredients against the allergens. If an ingredient matches exactly any of the three allergens, the dish is unsafe. Also, if an ingredient contains the word peanut as a substring, it is unsafe. Collect all safe dishes. Return a list of dish names that are safe to eat, sorted alphabetically.

title: Library Overdue Fine Calculator
spec: Write a function `fine(returns)` that calculates overdue fines for returned library books. The input is a list of tuples containing borrower name, days overdue, and a book category which is either standard, children, or reference. The fine rules are ten cents per day for standard books, five cents per day for children books, and fifty cents per day for reference books. If a book is more than thirty days overdue, an additional flat penalty of five dollars is added. Cap the maximum fine for any single book at ten dollars. Sum the total fines for each borrower. Return a list of tuples of borrower name and total fine in cents, sorted by highest fine first.

title: Weather Station Temperature Extremes
spec: Create a function `analyze(readings)` that finds the hottest and coldest days from a series of weather station reports. The input is a list of daily reports, each a tuple containing the day number and a list of hourly temperature integers. For each day, find the maximum and minimum temperatures. Calculate the daily average by summing the temperatures and dividing by the count. Identify the day with the highest maximum temperature and the day with the lowest minimum temperature. Return a tuple containing three items: the day number of the hottest day, the day number of the coldest day, and a list of daily averages sorted by day number.

title: Museum Tour Guide Scheduler
spec: Write a function `schedule(tours)` that assigns available tour guides to scheduled museum tours. The input is a list of tour tuples, each containing a start hour, end hour, and language required. The museum has three guides who speak english, two who speak spanish, and one who speaks french. Maintain a list of availability for each guide. When a tour requires a specific language, find an available guide who speaks that language and is free during the requested hours. A guide is free if they have no overlapping tours. If a guide is assigned, mark them busy. Return a count of how many tours successfully received a guide and how many were left without one as a tuple of two integers.

title: Student Quiz Grade Normalizer
spec: Create a function `grade(scores)` that normalizes student quiz results by dropping their lowest score. The input is a list of student records, each a tuple of student name and a list of five integer quiz scores. For each student, first check if any score is missing or negative; if so, replace it with a zero. Then, find the lowest score among the five and remove it. Calculate the sum of the remaining four scores. If the sum is greater than or equal to three hundred and sixty, award an honors status string. Return a list of tuples containing student name, the sum of their top four scores, and their status string which is either honors or regular, sorted alphabetically by student name.

title: Courier Route Delivery Optimizer
spec: Write a function `deliver(packages)` that calculates the total distance traveled by a courier delivering packages on a straight road. The input is a list of package destination mile markers which are integers. The courier starts at mile zero. First, split the packages into two lists: those going to mile markers less than fifty, and those going to fifty or beyond. The courier first delivers all packages less than fifty in ascending order, then returns to mile zero. After that, they deliver the remaining packages in ascending order and return to zero again. Compute the total distance driven by summing the distances between consecutive stops, including the trips back to zero. Return the total distance as an integer.

title: Real Estate Property Evaluator
spec: Create a function `appraise(properties)` that evaluates a list of houses and returns the best deals. Each property in the input list is a tuple containing the address string, price in thousands, number of bedrooms, and condition which is either excellent, good, or poor. Discard any properties that are in poor condition. For the remaining properties, calculate a value score by multiplying the number of bedrooms by fifty and subtracting the price. If the condition is excellent, add twenty to the score. Filter out any properties with a negative score. Return a list of address strings for the properties that have a score of zero or higher, sorted by score in descending order.

title: Spacecraft Fuel Consumption Modeler
spec: Write a function `simulate(maneuvers)` that models the fuel usage of a spacecraft. The input is a list of planned maneuvers, each a tuple of engine type and duration in seconds. The main engine burns ten units of fuel per second, while the thruster burns two units per second. The spacecraft starts with one thousand units of fuel. Process each maneuver in order. Deduct the fuel required from the total. If a maneuver requires more fuel than is currently available, only execute it for the duration that the remaining fuel allows, deduct all remaining fuel, and ignore all subsequent maneuvers. Return a tuple of the remaining fuel amount and the number of maneuvers fully completed.

title: Public Transit Fare Capper
spec: Create a function `cap(trips)` that implements a daily fare capping system for a transit card. The input is a list of trip tuples for a single day, each containing a boarding time in hours and a zone string which is either city or suburb. A city trip costs two dollars and a suburb trip costs three dollars. The daily cap is eight dollars. Accumulate the cost of each trip. If adding the full cost of a trip would push the daily total above eight dollars, only charge the difference up to eight dollars. Once the cap is reached, all subsequent trips cost zero. Return a list of the actual amounts charged for each trip in the original order.

title: Chess Tournament Standings
spec: Write a function `rank(results)` that calculates points and standings for players in a chess tournament. The input is a list of game results, each a tuple containing white player name, black player name, and the outcome which is either white, black, or draw. A win is worth three points, a draw is one point, and a loss is zero points. Initialize a tally for all players seen in the results. For each game, award points to the white and black players accordingly based on the outcome. Finally, compile a list of tuples containing the player name and their total points. Sort this list by points in descending order, resolving any ties by sorting names alphabetically, and return it.

title: Smartphone Battery Monitor
spec: Create a function `monitor(events)` that tracks a phone battery percentage over time based on screen usage and charging events. The battery starts at one hundred percent. The input events is a list of tuples, each containing an event type which is either screen, background, or charge, and a duration in minutes. Screen time drains two percent per minute, background drains one percent per minute, and charging restores five percent per minute. Apply each event sequentially. Clamp the battery percentage so it never drops below zero or goes above one hundred. If the battery reaches zero, it turns off and ignores any events until a charge event occurs. Return the final battery percentage.

title: Online Game Matchmaking Queue
spec: Write a function `match(players)` that pairs up players for a game based on their skill rating. The input is a list of player tuples, each containing a player name and an integer skill rating. Separate the players into three tiers: bronze for ratings under one thousand, silver for ratings up to two thousand, and gold for ratings above two thousand. Within each tier, sort the players by their exact rating in ascending order. Then, pair adjacent players in the sorted list. If a tier has an odd number of players, the highest rated player in that tier is left unpaired and must wait. Return a list of paired tuples containing two player names, followed by a list of names of waiting players.

title: Automated Warehouse Robot Dispatcher
spec: Create a function `dispatch(orders)` that routes a warehouse robot to pick items. The warehouse has aisles numbered one through ten. The input is a list of order tuples, each specifying the item name and aisle number. The robot starts at aisle one. Sort the orders by aisle number in ascending order to minimize backtracking. Iterate through the sorted orders. For each order, calculate the travel distance from the robot current location to the target aisle. Update the robot location. Accumulate the total distance traveled. If multiple items are in the same aisle, the distance to move between them is zero. Return a tuple of the total distance traveled and a list of the sorted item names.

title: Video Streaming Bandwidth Adjuster
spec: Write a function `adjust(logs)` that determines the appropriate streaming quality based on network speed fluctuations. The input is a list of network speed measurements in megabits per second. The stream starts at high quality. Iterate through the measurements. If the speed drops below five for three consecutive measurements, downgrade the quality to low. If the speed stays above twenty for three consecutive measurements, upgrade the quality to high. Otherwise, keep the quality the same. Track the quality string, either high or low, at each measurement step. Return a list of quality strings representing the state of the stream during each measurement period.

title: Pet Boarding Kennel Feeding Plan
spec: Create a function `feed(dogs)` that calculates the daily food requirement for dogs in a kennel. The input is a list of dog tuples, each containing the dog name, weight in pounds, and age in years. For each dog, the base food amount is two cups for every ten pounds of weight. If the dog is under one year old, multiply the base amount by one and a half to support growth. If the dog is over ten years old, reduce the base amount by ten percent for senior care. Round the final amount to the nearest whole cup. Return a list of tuples containing the dog name and their required cups of food, sorted alphabetically by dog name.

title: Highway Toll Booth Collector
spec: Write a function `toll(vehicles)` that computes toll charges for vehicles passing through a checkpoint. The input is a list of vehicle tuples, each with a license plate string, vehicle type which is either car, truck, or motorcycle, and a boolean indicating if they have a toll pass. Cars pay five dollars, motorcycles pay three, and trucks pay ten. If a vehicle has a pass, apply a twenty percent discount to their toll. Check the license plate length; if it is fewer than six characters, apply a one dollar surcharge after any discounts. Sum all the final charges. Return a tuple containing the total revenue collected and a count of how many vehicles used a pass.

title: Board Game Dice Roller Rules
spec: Create a function `roll(turns)` that processes a series of dice rolls for a board game character. The input is a list of turns, where each turn is a tuple of three integer dice results. For each turn, sum the three dice. If all three dice show the exact same number, it is a critical hit and the sum is doubled. If any die shows a one, the turn is a fumble and the total score for that turn becomes zero regardless of the other dice. Add the final score of each turn to a cumulative total. If the total exceeds one hundred, cap it at one hundred and stop processing further turns. Return the final cumulative score.

title: Airline Seat Upgrades
spec: Write a function `upgrade(passengers, seats)` that determines which travelers get a better cabin. The first parameter is a list of passenger tuples, each containing a name string, a cabin class string such as economy or premium, and a boolean for frequent flyer status. The second parameter is the integer number of available upgrade spots. Premium passengers have the highest priority for upgrading to business class, followed by economy passengers upgrading to premium. Within the same cabin class, frequent flyers always get priority over regular travelers. If there is still a tie, preserve the original sequence from the input list. Deduct one from the available spots for each successful upgrade until no spots remain. Return a list of names of those who were upgraded. For example, given a list with Bob in premium not frequent and Charlie in premium frequent, and one seat, Charlie wins.

title: Alternating Cipher Encoder
spec: Implement a function `encode(message, shift)` that applies a shifting substitution cipher to a string. The first parameter is the string to encode, and the second is the starting integer shift value. Iterate through each character of the text. If the character is a letter, shift it forward in the alphabet by the current shift amount, wrapping around from Z back to A while preserving its uppercase or lowercase format. If the character is a space, leave it unchanged but increment the shift amount by one for all subsequent letters. Any other punctuation or digits should be left unchanged and do not affect the shift amount. Return the fully encoded string. For example, providing the string hello world with a shift of one should result in ifmmp xpsme.

title: Recipe Nutrition Calculator
spec: Design a function `calculate(recipe, database)` that computes the total energy content of a meal. The first argument is a list of ingredient tuples, each containing a food name and the required portion size in grams. The second argument is a list of database tuples containing a food name and its energy value per hundred grams. To find the energy for an ingredient, search the database list for a matching name, then multiply its energy value by the required portion divided by one hundred. If an ingredient from the recipe is completely missing from the database, add its name to a separate missing items list and count its energy as zero. Return a tuple containing the total energy rounded to the nearest whole number, followed by the list of missing ingredient names. For example, an apple at two hundred grams with a database value of fifty per hundred grams yields one hundred total.

title: Highway Speed Violations
spec: Create a function `flag(records, limit)` that identifies speeding vehicles from traffic camera data. The first input is a list of camera records, where each is a tuple holding a license plate string, the distance traveled in kilometers, and the time taken in hours. The second input is the speed limit as a number. For each record, calculate the average speed by dividing the distance by the time. If this speed is strictly greater than the speed limit, note the vehicle as a violator. Calculate by how much they exceeded the limit. Sort the violators based on how much they exceeded the limit in descending order. If two vehicles exceeded it by the same amount, sort them alphabetically by their license plate. Return a list of the license plate strings of the violators. For example, a car traveling one hundred kilometers in half an hour has a speed of two hundred, which exceeds a limit of ninety.

title: Book Chapter Paginator
spec: Develop a function `paginate(chapters, capacity)` that calculates the total number of pages required to print a book. The first parameter is a list of integers representing the word count of each chapter in sequence. The second parameter is the maximum number of words that can fit on a single page. Each chapter must always start on a brand new page. For every chapter, divide its word count by the page capacity to find out how many pages it takes, rounding up to the nearest whole page. If a chapter has zero words, it still consumes exactly one blank page. Keep a running sum of all the pages used by every chapter. Return the total integer number of pages required for the entire book. For example, chapters of sizes ten and twenty with a capacity of fifteen will require one page for the first chapter and two pages for the second, totaling three pages.

title: Coffee Shop Loyalty Program
spec: Write a function `reward(purchases, threshold)` that tracks customer rewards for a local cafe. The first argument is a list of purchase tuples, each containing a customer name string and an integer for the number of coffees bought in that visit. The second argument is the integer number of coffees required to earn one free drink. A customer's purchases accumulate over multiple visits. Group the total coffees bought by each customer. Divide their total by the threshold to determine how many free drinks they have earned, rounding down. The remainder represents the coffees counting towards their next reward. Return a list of tuples, where each tuple contains the customer name, the number of free drinks earned, and the number of coffees needed to reach the next reward. Sort the result alphabetically by customer name. For example, if Alice buys seven coffees total and the threshold is five, her tuple will show one earned and two needed.

title: Disk Space Cleanup Manager
spec: Construct a function `cleanup(files, target)` that selects which old documents to delete to free up enough storage. The first argument is a list of file tuples, each containing a filename string, its size in megabytes, and the number of days since it was last accessed. The second argument is the integer target size to free up. First, filter out any files that have been accessed within the last thirty days, as they are too recent to delete. Sort the remaining candidate files primarily by their size in descending order, and secondarily by the number of days since last access in descending order to prefer deleting older files. Iterate through the sorted candidates and keep a running total of the size freed. Stop selecting files as soon as the running total meets or exceeds the target. Return a list of the selected filename strings. For example, if the target is fifty, select the largest available old files until at least fifty megabytes are cleared.

title: Payroll Overtime Calculator
spec: Develop a function `payroll(timesheets, rate)` to calculate weekly wages for employees. The timesheets parameter is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains an employee name and a list of seven numbers representing the hours they worked each day from Monday to Sunday. The rate parameter is their base hourly pay. Regular hours are capped at eight hours per day from Monday to Friday. Any hours beyond eight on a weekday are paid at one and a half times the base rate. All hours worked on Saturday or Sunday are paid at double the base rate, regardless of the daily total. Calculate the total pay for each employee by summing their regular, overtime, and weekend earnings. Return a list of tuples containing the employee name and their total calculated pay, sorted alphabetically by name. For example, an employee working ten hours on Monday earns eight regular hours and two overtime hours.

title: Fantasy RPG Combat Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(hero, monster)` that resolves a battle between two characters. Both arguments are tuples containing a name string, an integer for health points, an integer for attack power, an integer for defense, and an integer for speed. The character with the higher speed strikes first; in case of a tie, the hero goes first. During an attack, the damage dealt is the attacker's attack power minus the defender's defense, with a minimum of one damage point always being dealt. The defender's health is reduced by this damage. The combatants take turns attacking each other until one of their health points drops to zero or below. At that point, the battle ends immediately. Return a tuple containing the name of the victorious character and their remaining health points. For example, if a hero defeats a goblin without taking damage, return the hero name and their full original health.

title: Escape Room Time Evaluator
spec: Create a function `evaluate(puzzles, limit)` that determines if a team successfully beat an escape room. The puzzles argument is a list of performance tuples, each containing the base time in minutes spent on a specific puzzle and the integer number of hints requested for it. The limit argument is the maximum allowed total time in minutes. For each puzzle, calculate its effective time by adding the base time to a penalty of five minutes for every hint used on that puzzle. Sum the effective times of all puzzles to get the team's total completion time. If the total time is strictly less than or equal to the limit, the team successfully escapes. Return a tuple containing a boolean indicating if they escaped, followed by their total effective time. For example, a ten minute puzzle with two hints takes twenty minutes effectively.

title: Theme Park Ride Screener
spec: Design a function `screen(riders, rides)` that matches guests with appropriate attractions based on safety rules. The riders input is a list of tuples containing a guest name and their height in inches. The rides input is a list of tuples containing a ride name, the minimum required height, and the maximum allowed height. Some rides may not have a maximum height, represented by a zero. For each ride, determine which riders are tall enough to meet the minimum requirement and, if a maximum height exists, are also short enough to not exceed it. Gather the eligible guest names into a list for that ride. Return a list of these guest name lists, in the exact same order as the rides were provided. For example, if a guest is forty inches tall, they can ride the carousel which requires thirty inches, but not the coaster which requires fifty.

title: Plant Watering Scheduler
spec: Write a function `schedule(plants, current)` to identify which houseplants need attention today. The plants parameter is a list of tuples containing a plant name, the integer number of days required between waterings, and the integer day it was last watered. The current parameter is the integer representing today's day number. For each plant, calculate its next scheduled watering day by adding its watering interval to its last watered day. A plant needs to be watered if its scheduled day is exactly equal to the current day, or if the scheduled day is strictly less than the current day indicating it is overdue. Collect the names of all plants that need watering. Sort these names alphabetically and return the resulting list. For example, a fern last watered on day ten with an interval of three needs watering on or after day thirteen.

title: Bakery Order Fulfillment
spec: Implement a function `fulfill(stock, orders)` that processes requested baked goods based on available supplies. The stock parameter is a list of tuples containing an ingredient name and its available quantity in grams. The orders parameter is a list of tuples containing a customer name and a list of required ingredient tuples for their order. First, summarize the stock into a running inventory tracker. Then, process the orders sequentially in the exact order they appear. For each order, check if there is enough of every required ingredient in the inventory. If all requirements are met, deduct the quantities from the inventory and add the customer name to a success list. If even one ingredient is insufficient, reject the entire order and leave the inventory unchanged for that order. Return a list of the names of customers whose orders were successfully fulfilled.

title: Postal Zip Code Sorter
spec: Develop a function `distribute(packages)` that groups mail items into regional bins based on their destination. The packages parameter is a list of strings representing zip codes. There are ten regional bins numbered zero through nine. To determine the correct bin for a package, look at the very first character of its zip code. If the zip code is empty, entirely spaces, or does not start with a digit, it is invalid and should be sent to a special unclassified pile. Otherwise, place it into the bin corresponding to its starting digit. After processing all packages, construct a list of ten integers representing the count of packages in each bin from zero to nine. Return a tuple containing this list of counts and an integer for the total number of unclassified packages. For example, a zip code starting with four adds one to the tally for bin four.

title: Music Festival Stage Assigner
spec: Create a function `assign(bands, stages)` that schedules musical acts across different venues. The bands argument is a list of tuples containing a band name and their required set length in minutes. The stages argument is a list of available venue times in minutes. Maintain a tracker of the remaining time for each stage. Process the bands in the order they are listed. Attempt to place each band on the first available stage that has enough remaining time to host their full set. If a suitable stage is found, deduct the band's set length from that stage's remaining time and record the assignment. If no stage can accommodate the band, they are left off the schedule. Return a list of lists, where each inner list contains the names of the bands assigned to that particular stage, in the order the stages were provided.

title: Paint Batch Blender
spec: Write a function `blend(batches)` that calculates the final color produced by mixing multiple quantities of paint. The batches parameter is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains the integer values for red, green, blue, and the total volume of that batch in liters. To find the blended color, calculate the volume-weighted total for each color component. Multiply the red value by the volume for each batch and sum these products, then do the same for green and blue. Keep track of the overall total volume by summing the individual batch volumes. Finally, divide the accumulated totals for red, green, and blue by the overall total volume, rounding each result down to the nearest integer. Return a tuple of the three resulting integers representing the final red, green, and blue values. If the batch list is empty, return zeros for all three colors.

title: Candidate Interview Scorer
spec: Implement a function `score(answers, threshold)` to evaluate potential hires based on their technical responses. The answers input is a list of tuples, each containing a question weight integer and an awarded score out of ten. The threshold input is the minimum required weighted average to pass. First, iterate through the answers and calculate the total possible weighted maximum and the actual weighted score achieved by multiplying each score by its weight. Compute the final percentage score by dividing the achieved score by the maximum possible score and multiplying by one hundred. Furthermore, check if the candidate received a score strictly less than three on any single question. If they have such a critically low score on any question, they automatically fail the interview. Otherwise, they pass if their final percentage is equal to or greater than the threshold. Return a boolean indicating if they pass.

title: Greenhouse Temperature Regulator
spec: Design a function `regulate(readings, limits)` that monitors environmental controls over a day. The readings parameter is a list of observed temperatures. The limits parameter is a tuple containing a minimum threshold, a maximum threshold, and an ideal target temperature. The greenhouse has a heater and a cooler, both initially off. For each reading, check the status. If the temperature drops strictly below the minimum, turn the heater on and the cooler off. If the temperature rises strictly above the maximum, turn the cooler on and the heater off. If either device is currently on and the temperature reaches exactly the ideal target, turn both devices off. Count how many total transitions from off to on occur for the heater, and similarly for the cooler. Return a tuple containing the heater activation count and the cooler activation count.

title: Marathon Pacing Calculator
spec: Develop a function `pace(target, splits, distance)` that determines the required speed for a runner to achieve their goal. The target parameter is the total desired finish time in minutes. The splits parameter is a list of times in minutes taken for each kilometer completed so far. The distance parameter is the total race length in kilometers. Sum the provided splits to find the total time elapsed. Count the number of splits to determine the distance already covered. Subtract the elapsed time from the target time to find the remaining time available. Subtract the covered distance from the total distance to find the remaining kilometers. If the remaining distance is zero or the remaining time is negative, return zero. Otherwise, divide the remaining time by the remaining distance to calculate the required pace per kilometer. Return this required pace rounded to two decimal places.

title: Podcast Advertisement Selector
spec: Write a function `monetize(duration, ads)` that chooses commercials to maximize show revenue. The duration parameter is the total length of the podcast episode in minutes. A podcast can feature exactly one advertisement slot for every full fifteen minutes of content. The ads parameter is a list of tuples, each containing an ad title, its length in seconds, and its monetary payout. Sort the available ads based on their payout in descending order, and in case of a tie, by their length in ascending order. Determine the maximum number of allowed ad slots by dividing the podcast duration by fifteen and rounding down. Iterate through the sorted ads and select them one by one until the number of selected ads reaches the allowed slot limit. Return a list of the titles of the chosen advertisements.

title: Astronomy Star Catalog Filter
spec: Create a function `extract(stars, distance, brightness)` that isolates specific celestial objects from a database. The stars parameter is a list of tuples containing a star name string, its distance from Earth in lightyears, and its visual magnitude where a lower number means a brighter star. The distance parameter is the maximum allowed distance, and the brightness parameter is the highest allowed magnitude value. Iterate through the list of stars and examine their properties. Keep only the stars whose distance is less than or equal to the maximum allowed distance, and whose visual magnitude is less than or equal to the brightness threshold. Sort the filtered stars by their visual magnitude in ascending order so that the brightest stars appear first. If two stars have the exact same magnitude, sort them alphabetically by their name. Return a list of the filtered star names.

title: Vocabulary Flashcard Review
spec: Implement a function `review(cards, results)` that updates spaced repetition learning progress. The cards parameter is a list of tuples containing a vocabulary word and its current correct streak as an integer. The results parameter is a list of tuples containing a word and a boolean indicating if the user remembered it correctly during the test. For each test result, locate the corresponding word in the flashcards. If the user was correct, increment the streak for that word by exactly one. If the user was incorrect, reset the streak for that word to zero. If a word from the results does not exist in the flashcards, ignore it. Once all results have been processed, sort the updated flashcards primarily by their current streak in ascending order, and secondarily by the word alphabetically. Return a list of tuples representing the updated flashcards.

title: Car Wash Service Queue
spec: Develop a function `service(vehicles, capacity)` to simulate a car wash operation. The vehicles parameter is a list of tuples containing a customer name, a vehicle type string which is either car or truck, and a boolean for premium wash. The capacity parameter is the integer maximum minutes available. A standard car wash takes ten minutes, while a standard truck wash takes fifteen minutes. If a premium wash is requested, add five minutes to the base time. Process the vehicles in the sequence they arrived. If starting a vehicle's wash would exceed the remaining available capacity time, turn that vehicle away and immediately halt operations for the day, ignoring any remaining vehicles in the line. Return a list of the names of customers whose vehicles were successfully washed before time ran out.

title: Fitness Challenge Leaderboard
spec: Write a function `rank(participants, target)` that evaluates a step counting competition. The participants parameter is a list of tuples containing a team name and a list of seven integers representing daily step counts for a week. The target parameter is the weekly team step goal. For each team, sum their daily steps to find the weekly total. Calculate their consistency by counting how many individual days they achieved at least ten thousand steps. A team qualifies for the leaderboard only if their weekly total meets or exceeds the target goal. Sort the qualified teams first by their weekly total steps in descending order, then by their consistency count in descending order. Return a list of tuples containing the team name, their total steps, and their consistency count for all qualified teams.

title: Food Truck Menu Selector
spec: Design a function `select(dishes, budget)` that picks the best combination of meals for a catered event. The dishes parameter is a list of tuples containing a dish name, its cost per serving, and its popularity score out of ten. The budget parameter is the maximum total cost allowed. To maximize satisfaction, sort the available dishes based on their popularity score in descending order. In case of a tie, sort by cost in ascending order. Iterate through the sorted dishes and add them to your selected menu one by one, deducting their cost from the remaining budget. Only add a dish if its cost is less than or equal to the currently available budget. A dish can only be added once. Return a list of the names of the chosen dishes in the order they were selected.

title: Email Spam Filter Simulation
spec: Write a function `filter(messages)` that takes a list of message strings and returns a list of classification strings, either spam or valid.
