A message is considered spam if it contains the word free in uppercase more than two times, consists of more than fifty percent uppercase letters overall ignoring spaces, or contains three or more exclamation marks in a row. Additionally, any message shorter than ten characters is automatically marked as spam. Valid messages are those that pass all these checks. Include a small driver block that processes a list of mixed messages and prints the totals for each category. Example: an input of a list containing a short message, a normal message, and a message with too many exclamation marks yields a list containing spam, valid, spam.

title: Package Sorting Facility
spec: Write a function `sort(packages)` that takes a list of tuples containing length, width, height, and weight and returns a list of assigned destination strings. A package is bulky if any single dimension is greater than or equal to 150 centimeters, or if the volume is greater than 1000000 cubic centimeters. A package is heavy if its weight is greater than or equal to 20 kilograms. Packages that are both bulky and heavy go to the rejected queue. Packages that are either bulky or heavy go to the special queue, while all other packages go to the standard queue. The logic must calculate volume and check dimensions for each item. Example: an input of a list of tuples like (10, 10, 10, 5) and (200, 10, 10, 25) yields standard, rejected.

title: Course Prerequisite Checker
spec: Write a function `verify(records, requirements)` that takes a list of student records and a list of course requirements to determine who can graduate. Each student record is a tuple of a name and a list of completed course names. Each course requirement is a tuple of a course name and a list of prerequisite course names. To graduate, a student must have completed at least four courses in total, and for every course they have taken, they must also have completed all its prerequisites. Return a list of names of students who are eligible to graduate. Include a small driver that sets up a mock curriculum and student list to test the logic. Example: if a student has taken basic math and advanced math, and advanced math requires basic math, they are valid but need two more courses to graduate.

title: Crafting Material Cost Evaluator
spec: Write a function `cost(blueprints, prices)` that evaluates the total price to forge various items, where blueprints is a list of tuples containing an item name and a list of required material names. The second parameter is a list of price tuples, each containing a material name and its integer cost. If a blueprint contains a material not present in the prices list, it is skipped entirely. If the total cost of a valid blueprint is strictly less than 15, it is classified as budget, otherwise it is premium. Return a list of tuples containing the blueprint name, the total integer cost, and the classification string. Include a helper to sum the materials and a main block to define sample data. Example: an input of an iron sword blueprint needing iron and leather, given prices of 5 and 3, returns a list with a tuple of iron sword, 8, budget.

title: Ferry Route Freight Accumulator
spec: Write a function `charge(manifests)` that processes marine transport records to calculate total shipping fees. Each manifest is a tuple containing a vessel name string, a cargo type string, and an integer distance traveled in nautical miles. Grains are charged 2 per mile, machinery is charged 5 per mile, and textiles are charged 1 per mile. If the manifest distance exceeds 50 miles, a ten percent discount is applied to the total fee for that specific trip, rounded down to the nearest integer. If the cargo type is emergency relief, an additional flat discount of 5 is subtracted, but the final fee cannot drop below zero. Return a list of tuples grouping each unique vessel name with its total accumulated integer fee across all trips. Example: a grain shipment of 10 miles yields 20, and a machinery shipment of 60 miles yields 270.

title: Lift Capacity Grouping
spec: Write a function `load(passengers, capacity)` that groups waiting people into elevator trips. The first parameter is a list of passenger weights as integers, and the second is the maximum integer weight the elevator can hold. Passengers must board in the exact order they appear in the list. For each passenger, if adding them to the current trip exceeds the capacity, the current trip is finalized and they become the first person in the next trip. If a single passenger exceeds the capacity on their own, they are placed in a trip by themselves but flagged with an overcapacity warning string instead of their weight. Return a list of trips, where each trip is a list of passenger weights or warning strings, and include a main driver to execute the loading process on sample waiting lines. Example: weights of 50, 80, and 60 with a capacity of 100 yields three trips, the first with 50, the second with 80, and the third with 60.

title: Holiday Gift Exchange Assignment
spec: Write a function `assign(participants)` that determines a valid secret santa drawing for a group. The input is a list of strings representing participant names. The algorithm must pair each person with exactly one other person to give a gift to, and no one can be assigned to themselves. To achieve a reproducible result without randomness, shift each participant to the one sitting two spots to their right in a circular manner. If the list has fewer than three people, return an empty list because a proper assignment cannot be made. Return a list of pairs, where each pair is a tuple of the giver name and the receiver name. Example: an input of Alice, Bob, Charlie, and Diana yields pairs where Alice gives to Charlie, Bob gives to Diana, Charlie gives to Alice, and Diana gives to Bob.

title: Golf Handicap Adjuster
spec: Write a function `adjust(golfers)` that calculates competitive adjustments for a golf league. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains a player name string and a list of integer scores from their recent rounds. First, find the average score for each player, ignoring any scores above 120 as they represent incomplete or scratched rounds. If a player has no valid rounds, their average is set to 100. The handicap is calculated as ninety percent of the difference between the player average and 72, rounded down to the nearest integer, but if the average is 72 or lower, the handicap is 0. Return a list of tuples containing the player name and their integer handicap, structuring the solution with a helper for the average calculation and a driver block. Example: a player with valid scores of 90 and 94 gets a handicap of 18.

title: Smart Home Lighting Schedule Evaluator
spec: Write a function `illuminate(events)` that processes home motion and timer events to determine if the lights should be on or off. The input is a list of tuples containing an integer hour from 0 to 23, a room name, and an event type string which is either motion or timer. Lights turn on if there is motion between 18 and 23, or between 0 and 5. A timer event always turns the lights off regardless of the time. If multiple events occur in the same hour for the same room, the last event in the sequence determines the final state for that hour. Return a list of tuples containing the hour, the room name, and the final state string which is either on or off. Example: an input of hour 19, living room, motion followed by hour 19, living room, timer results in a state of off for that hour.

title: Gym Class Attendance Tracking
spec: Write a function `attend(logs, capacity)` that manages signups for fitness sessions. The logs parameter is a list of tuples containing a member name and a class name. The capacity parameter is an integer representing the maximum number of people allowed per class. Process the logs in order; if a class is already at full capacity, the member is placed on a waitlist for that class. If a member tries to sign up for a class they are already enrolled in, the duplicate entry is ignored. Return a list of tuples containing the class name, a list of enrolled member names, and a list of waitlisted member names. Example: with capacity 1, signing up Alice for yoga, then Bob for yoga, yields yoga with Alice enrolled and Bob waitlisted.

title: Overdue Invoice Penalty Calculator
spec: Write a function `penalize(invoices, rates)` that computes monetary penalties for late payments. The first input is a list of tuples containing a client name, an invoice ID, and an integer representing days overdue. The second input is a list of tuples containing a client name and their integer daily penalty rate. For every invoice that is overdue by more than 15 days, a penalty is calculated at a flat 50 units plus the daily rate for every integer day past the 15 day grace period. Speeds that exceed the limit by more than 20 miles per hour incur an additional reckless driving surcharge of 50 units, but wait, let me rephrase that. Invoices overdue by more than 60 days incur an additional severe delinquency surcharge of 200 units, but if the client is missing from the rates list, skip the invoice entirely. Return a list of tuples grouping each client name with their total accumulated penalties. Example: an invoice 25 days overdue for a client with a daily rate of 5 yields a penalty of 100.

title: Project Milestone Progress Bar Generator
spec: Write a function `progress(milestones)` that creates visual text bars representing project completion. The input is a list of tuples containing a project name, an integer for completed tasks, and an integer for total tasks. Calculate the percentage of completion, capping it at 100 if completed tasks exceed total tasks. The visual bar must be exactly ten characters long, using the hash character for each full ten percent completed, and a dash character for the remaining segments. If total tasks is zero, the bar should be entirely dashes. Return a list of tuples containing the project name, the percentage as an integer rounded down, and the visual bar string, and include a small driver to test sample projects. Example: an input of alpha, 5, 10 yields a tuple of alpha, 50, and a string of 5 hashes followed by 5 dashes.

title: Library Shelf Space Allocator
spec: Write a function `shelve(books, limit)` that distributes a stack of books across multiple shelves. The books parameter is a list of integer page counts, and the limit parameter is the maximum total pages a single shelf can hold. Books are processed in the order they appear. If a book has more pages than the limit itself, it is sent to the oversize collection and does not take up shelf space. Otherwise, keep adding books to the current shelf until adding the next book would exceed the limit, at which point a new shelf is started. Return a list of shelves, where each shelf is a list of book page counts, and append the oversize collection as the final list if it contains any books. Example: books of sizes 200, 300, and 500 with a limit of 400 yields three lists.

title: Treasure Hunt Sequence Validator
spec: Write a function `clue(steps, sequence)` that evaluates a team attempt at solving a puzzle. The steps parameter is a list of valid string actions required in exact order to win, and the sequence parameter is a list of string actions actually taken by the team. Iterate through the team sequence to see how many valid steps they complete, counting an action only if it matches the current required step. Incorrect actions add a 5 minute penalty each, but do not reset progress. If the team finishes all required steps before the sequence ends, any remaining actions are ignored and they succeed. Return a tuple containing a boolean of whether they succeeded, the integer number of completed steps, and the total integer penalty minutes. Example: requiring pull, twist and getting push, pull, twist gives true, 2 steps complete, and 5 penalty minutes.

title: Retail Return Policy Enforcer
spec: Write a function `refund(returns)` that determines the refund status of purchased items. The input is a list of tuples containing an item name, an integer days since purchase, a boolean indicating if the receipt is present, and a condition string which is either new or used. A full refund is granted if the item is in new condition, has a receipt, and is returned within 30 days. Store credit is given if the item is used but returned within 14 days with a receipt. Items without a receipt are strictly rejected, and items exceeding 90 days since purchase are rejected regardless of condition. Return a list of tuples containing the item name and the resulting action string which can be full, credit, or rejected. Example: a new item returned at 20 days with a receipt yields full.

title: Aquarium Tank Compatibility Checker
spec: Write a function `compatible(fishes)` that groups aquatic creatures into separate tanks based on their traits. The input is a list of tuples containing a fish name, a behavior string either peaceful or aggressive, and a water type string either fresh or salt. Aggressive fish cannot share a tank with any peaceful fish, and freshwater and saltwater fish must be kept in completely separate tanks. When processing the list, place each fish into the first existing tank that satisfies these safety rules. If no current tank is suitable, start a new tank for that fish. Return a list of tanks, where each tank is a list of fish names, and use a helper routine to verify tank safety rules. Example: a peaceful fresh fish, an aggressive fresh fish, and a peaceful salt fish will result in three distinct tanks.

title: Ski Resort Lift Ticket Pricing
spec: Write a function `price(skiers)` that calculates daily lift pass costs based on age and purchase timing. The input is a list of tuples containing a skier name, their integer age, and an integer days in advance the ticket was bought. The base price for an adult is 80, while children under 12 pay 40, and seniors 65 or older pay 50. If the ticket was purchased more than 30 days in advance, a twenty percent discount is applied to the final price. If it was purchased on the same day, indicated by 0 days, a 10 unit premium is added. Return a list of tuples containing the skier name and the final integer price rounded down. Example: a 10 year old booking 0 days in advance pays 50.

title: Hotel Room Cleaning Schedule
spec: Write a function `clean(rooms)` that prioritizes hotel housekeeping tasks. The input is a list of tuples containing a room number string, a boolean indicating if the guest is checking out, and an integer representing the days since the room was last cleaned. A room must be cleaned today if the guest is checking out, or if it has been more than 3 days since the last cleaning. Check out rooms are high priority, while stay over rooms are low priority. Rooms that do not meet the criteria are skipped entirely. Return a list containing two lists: the first holds the room numbers for high priority cleaning, and the second holds the room numbers for low priority cleaning. Example: a checkout room last cleaned 1 day ago goes into the high priority list, and a stay over room cleaned 4 days ago goes into the low priority list.

title: Chemical Solution Diluter
spec: Write a function `dilute(solutions, factor)` that multiplies laboratory requirements and converts units. The solutions parameter is a list of tuples containing a chemical name, an integer quantity, and a unit string which is either milliliters or drops. The factor parameter is an integer multiplier. First, multiply the quantity of each chemical by the factor. Then, if a chemical measured in drops reaches 20 or more, convert the whole amount into milliliters by dividing by 20, leaving any remainder in a separate new entry as drops. Return a list of tuples with the chemical name, the new integer quantity, and the unit string, including a helper for the unit conversion. Example: 5 drops multiplied by 6 yields one tuple of 1 milliliter and another tuple of 10 drops for that chemical.

title: Vehicle Parking Billing
spec: Write a function `park(tickets, rate)` that processes parking duration to calculate charges. The tickets parameter is a list of tuples containing a license plate string and an integer minutes parked. The rate parameter is an integer representing the cost per full hour. Any partial hour is rounded up to the next full hour for billing purposes, and the maximum charge for a single day is capped at 10 times the hourly rate. If a vehicle is parked for less than 15 minutes, it falls within the grace period and is charged 0. Return a list of tuples containing the license plate and the final integer fee. Example: a car parked for 65 minutes at a rate of 5 is charged 10, while a car parked for 10 minutes is charged 0.

title: Solar Panel Dust Accumulator
spec: Write a function `wash(panels, rain)` that determines which energy modules need manual cleaning. The panels parameter is a list of tuples containing a panel ID string, an integer dust tolerance in grams, and a boolean indicating if it is shielded from weather. The rain parameter is an integer representing recent natural rain cleaning power in grams. If a panel is shielded, it receives no natural rain and must be manually cleaned for its full dust tolerance. For unshielded panels, subtract the rain from their tolerance; if the result is greater than zero, that difference is the manual cleaning amount, otherwise it needs 0. Return a list of tuples containing the panel ID and the integer manual cleaning amount. Example: an unshielded panel needing 20 grams of cleaning after 10 grams of rain needs 10 manual.

title: Book Reading Marathon Tracker
spec: Write a function `read(chapters, speed)` that estimates how many chapters can be finished in a given time. The chapters parameter is a list of integer page counts for consecutive chapters, and the speed parameter is an integer representing pages read per hour. Assume the reading session lasts for exactly 4 hours. Iterate through the chapters and subtract their page counts from the total pages the reader can complete in the session. If a chapter can only be partially completed before time runs out, count it as a fraction and stop the process. Return a tuple containing the integer number of fully completed chapters and the remaining unread pages from the partially completed chapter. Example: at 50 pages an hour for 4 hours, chapters of 80, 70, and 60 yield 2 completed chapters and 50 pages left in the third.

title: Snack Dispenser Tracker
spec: Write a function `vend(selections, stock)` that simulates dispensing snacks and tracks shortages. The selections parameter is a list of strings representing the items chosen by a user in sequence. The stock parameter is a list of tuples containing an item name and its starting integer quantity. For each selection, if the item is in stock and has a quantity greater than zero, decrement its quantity and record it as dispensed. If the item is out of stock or completely missing from the stock list, record it as missed. Return a tuple containing a list of dispensed item strings and a list of missed item strings. Example: selecting chips twice when only 1 chips is in stock yields one dispensed chips and one missed chips.

title: Auditorium Group Placement
spec: Write a function `seat(groups, rows)` that allocates parties to a cinema auditorium. The groups parameter is a list of integer party sizes. The rows parameter is an integer representing the uniform number of empty seats in each row, and the theater has 10 rows in total. Process each group in order to find the first available row from front to back that has enough consecutive empty seats for the group, and subtract their size from that row's capacity. If no single row can accommodate the entire group, they are turned away and not seated. Return a tuple containing the integer number of seated individuals and a list of integers representing the remaining capacity of each of the 10 rows. Example: groups of 4 and 3 into rows of 5 leaves one row with 1 seat and another with 2 seats.

title: Security Credential Screener
spec: Write a function `validate(passwords)` that checks strings for security compliance. The input is a list of password strings. A password is considered strong if it is at least 8 characters long, contains at least one numeric digit, and contains at least one uppercase letter. If a password contains the word password in any mixture of cases, it is immediately deemed weak regardless of other criteria. If a password meets the length requirement but lacks either a digit or an uppercase letter, it is classified as medium. Return a list of tuples containing the original password and its classification string which can be strong, medium, or weak, including a driver to evaluate a batch of mock passwords. Example: a password of secret123 is medium because it lacks an uppercase letter, while Password123 is weak due to the forbidden word.

title: Object Graph to XML Serializer
spec: Write a function `serialize(data)` that takes a list of dictionaries representing elements and converts them into an XML string representation. Each dictionary has a tag name string, an optional dictionary of string attributes, and an optional list of children which can be strings or further element dictionaries. The function should recursively process the elements, formatting them with angle brackets. If an element has no children, it should be rendered as a self closing tag. For example, passing a list with one dictionary having a tag of document and a child string of text should return the appropriate XML tags enclosing the word text.

title: Indented Text Tree Parser
spec: Write a function `parse(lines)` that takes a list of strings representing lines of text, where hierarchy is indicated by leading tabs. The function must build a list of nested tuples. Each string without leading tabs is a root node. If a line has one more tab than the previous line, it becomes a child of the previous line. The function must iterate through the lines, counting the leading tabs, and use a stack to maintain the current path. If a line has fewer tabs, the stack should pop elements until the correct parent is found. Blank lines should be skipped. For example, a root line followed by a line with one tab containing child should return a list containing a tuple of root and a list of its children.

title: Chat Intent Router
spec: Write a function `route(messages)` that takes a list of user message strings and determines the appropriate department route for each. The function must check for specific keywords in each message. If a message contains buy, cost, or price, route to sales. If it contains break, error, or bug, route to support. If it contains return, refund, or cancel, route to billing. If a message matches multiple categories, prioritize support over billing and sales. If no keywords match, route to general. The function must return a list of department string names corresponding to the input messages. For example, passing a list with one message asking for a refund should return a list containing the word billing.

title: Diagnostic Trace Aggregator
spec: Write a function `summarize(traces)` that takes a list of strings representing system events. Each string starts with a timestamp, followed by a severity level, and a description separated by spaces. The function must parse each line, filter out any event that is not an error or critical level, and extract the description. It should count the occurrences of each unique description using a dictionary. Finally, the function must return a list of tuples containing the description and its count, sorted descending by count. For example, passing a list with two identical error events and one info event should return a list with one tuple showing the error description and a count of two.

title: Mathematical Grouping Verifier
spec: Write a function `validate(sequence)` that takes a string of brackets including parentheses, square brackets, and curly braces. The function must determine if the sequence is balanced. It should iterate over the characters, pushing opening brackets onto a stack. When a closing bracket is encountered, it must check if the stack is empty and if the top of the stack is the matching opening bracket. If a mismatch is found, or if the stack is not empty at the end, the function should return the index of the first invalid character or the length of the string if the error is at the end. If valid, return negative one. For example, passing a string with an unclosed opening parenthesis should return one.

title: Forum Post Text Decorator
spec: Write a function `format(text)` that processes a string of text and applies basic styling. It should split the text into lines and process each line. If a line starts with a hash character and a space, it should be wrapped in heading tags. If a line starts with an asterisk and a space, it should be treated as a list item and wrapped in list item tags, with an unordered list block wrapping consecutive list items. Blank lines should be ignored. The function must accumulate the formatted lines and return them joined by newline characters. For example, passing a string with a heading line should return the text enclosed in a heading tag.

title: Relational Data Joiner
spec: Write a function `join(tables)` that takes a tuple containing two lists of records. Each record is a tuple of strings. The first string in each record is the identifier. The function must perform an inner join on the identifier. It should first iterate through the first list, storing records in a dictionary mapped by their identifier. Then, it should iterate through the second list. If the identifier from the second list exists in the dictionary, the function should concatenate the elements from both records, excluding the duplicate identifier, and add the combined record to a result list. For example, matching records with the same identifier should yield a new record containing data from both.

title: Linear Equation Variable Solver
spec: Write a function `solve(equations)` that takes a list of strings representing simple equations in the form of variable equals integer. Some equations may refer to other variables, like a equals b. The function must determine the integer value for every variable. It should iterate through the equations, storing integer values in a dictionary. For variables that point to other variables, it should add them to a waiting list. The function must loop through the waiting list until all variables are resolved to an integer. If a cycle is detected, return an empty list. Otherwise, return a list of tuples with the variable and its integer value, sorted alphabetically. For example, if x equals ten and y equals x, it should return tuples showing ten for both.

title: Text Keyword Highlighter
spec: Write a function `highlight(document)` that takes a tuple containing a text string and a list of target words. The function must find all occurrences of the target words in the text, ignoring upper and lower case differences, and enclose them in asterisk characters. It should split the text into words, keeping punctuation intact. For each word, it must strip punctuation, check if the lower case version exists in the target list, and if so, wrap the core word in asterisks while reattaching the punctuation. The function must return the reconstructed text string. For example, highlighting the word apple in a sentence should return the sentence with apple flanked by asterisks.

title: Sensor Telemetry Smoother
spec: Write a function `smooth(readings)` that takes a list of float numbers representing consecutive sensor readings. The function must eliminate spikes by replacing any reading that differs from its predecessor by more than twenty percent with a smoothed value. The smoothed value is the average of the previous reading and the next reading. If the spike occurs at the very end of the list, replace it with the previous reading. The function should iterate through the list using an index, build a new list of filtered values, and return it. For example, a list of ten, ten, fifty, and ten should return ten, ten, ten, and ten.

title: Contact Directory Merger
spec: Write a function `merge(contacts)` that takes a list of tuples representing individuals, where each tuple contains a string name, a string email, and a string phone number. The function must identify duplicates where either the email or the phone number matches an existing entry. It should maintain a list of merged contacts. For each incoming contact, it must check against the merged list. If a match is found, it updates the existing entry by filling in any missing information but retains the earliest name. If no match is found, the contact is added as a new entry. The function returns the deduplicated list. For example, two entries with the same email but different phone numbers should become one entry with both numbers.

title: System Options Stringifier
spec: Write a function `generate(settings)` that takes a list of tuples where each tuple has a section string, a key string, and a value string or integer. The function must produce a formatted configuration string. It should iterate over the tuples, grouping them by the section string into a dictionary of lists. Then, it should iterate over the dictionary alphabetically by section name. For each section, it prints the section name enclosed in square brackets. Underneath, it prints each key and value separated by an equals sign. The function should return the complete string joined by newlines. For example, passing settings for a database host should return the host key under the database section.

title: Daily Agenda Overlap Checker
spec: Write a function `detect(appointments)` that takes a list of tuples, where each tuple contains an event name, an integer start hour, and an integer end hour. The function must find all overlapping events. It should sort the list based on the start hour. Then, it must iterate through the sorted list, comparing each event to the previously processed events. If the start hour of the current event is less than the end hour of a previous event, a conflict is recorded. The function must return a list of names of events that overlap with any other event. For example, an event from one to three and an event from two to four should both be included in the returned list.

title: Portfolio Asset Rebalancer
spec: Write a function `rebalance(portfolio)` that takes a tuple containing a list of current asset tuples and a list of target percentage tuples. The current assets consist of an asset name string and a float value. The target percentages consist of an asset name string and a float target ratio. The function must calculate the total value of all current assets. It then determines the target value for each asset based on the target ratio. By comparing the current value to the target value, it calculates the difference to buy or sell. The function returns a list of tuples with the asset name and the adjustment amount. For example, if an asset is under its target value, it returns a positive adjustment.

title: Urban Vehicle Flow Manager
spec: Write a function `coordinate(traffic)` that takes a list of tuples representing queues of cars at four directions north, south, east, and west. Each tuple has the direction string and an integer for the number of cars waiting. The function must determine the sequence of green lights. It should prioritize directions with more than ten cars. If multiple directions have more than ten, it alternates between them in alphabetical order. Directions with fewer cars are processed only when all high traffic queues drop below five. It subtracts five cars per green light cycle. The function returns a list of direction strings in the order they were given a green light. For example, a heavy north queue will appear multiple times before a small east queue.

title: Dietary Recipe Substituter
spec: Write a function `substitute(ingredients)` that takes a list of string ingredient names. The function must replace certain ingredients based on dietary rules. It iterates through the list. If it finds milk or cheese, it replaces them with soy milk or vegan cheese respectively, unless the list also contains beef, in which case it leaves them alone. If it finds sugar, it replaces it with honey. If an ingredient is not recognized as needing substitution, it remains unchanged. The function should return the modified list of ingredients. For example, a list containing milk and sugar should return soy milk and honey.

title: Routing Path Cost Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(paths)` that takes a list of tuples representing network jumps, where each tuple contains a string origin, a string destination, and an integer latency cost. The function must find the total latency for continuous paths. It should link the jumps together by matching the destination of one jump to the origin of the next. If a continuous path forms a closed loop, the function should stop and record the total cost up to that point. It returns a list of tuples containing the starting origin and the total latency for each evaluated path. For example, three connected jumps with costs of ten each should yield a total cost of thirty.

title: Web Store Coupon Evaluator
spec: Write a function `calculate(cart)` that takes a tuple containing a list of item prices and a string promo code. The function must compute the final total. It first sums the prices. If the sum is greater than one hundred, it applies a ten percent discount to the total. Then, it evaluates the promo code. If the code is save twenty, it subtracts twenty from the total. If the code is half off, it cuts the total in half, but this cannot be combined with the volume discount, so it rolls back the ten percent first. The function must ensure the total never drops below zero and returns the final integer amount. For example, a cart of fifty with a save twenty code should return thirty.

title: Factory Part Quality Sorter
spec: Write a function `sort(parts)` that takes a list of tuples representing manufactured items, each with a string material type, an integer weight, and an integer defect count. The function must categorize each item into bins. If the defect count is above three, the item goes to scrap. If the defect count is zero and the weight is exactly fifty, it goes to premium. Otherwise, if the material is metal, it goes to heavy duty, and if plastic, it goes to standard. The function should iterate through the parts, append the category string to a result list, and return that list. For example, a flawless metal part weighing fifty returns premium.

title: Digital Book Chapter Indexer
spec: Write a function `index(pages)` that takes a list of strings representing page contents. The function must generate a table of contents. It loops through each page using a page number counter starting at one. On each page, it splits the text by newlines and examines each line. If a line starts with the word chapter followed by a space and a number, it extracts the entire line as the title. The function stores the title and the current page number in a tuple. Once all pages are processed, it returns a list of these tuples. For example, finding a chapter one text on the fifth page returns a tuple of the title and five.

title: Weekly Meal Calorie Balancer
spec: Write a function `balance(meals)` that takes a list of tuples containing a string day, a string meal type, and an integer calorie count. The function must calculate the daily total calories. It iterates over the meals and accumulates the calories per day using a dictionary. After totaling, it iterates over the daily totals. If a day exceeds two thousand calories, it calculates the excess amount. If a day is under one thousand five hundred, it calculates the deficit. The function returns a list of tuples containing the day string and a string describing it as either high, low, or normal. For example, a day with three thousand calories returns a tuple with the day and the word high.

title: Competition Bracket Seeder
spec: Write a function `seed(players)` that takes a list of tuples containing a string player name and an integer skill rating. The function must organize players into first round matches. It first sorts the players by skill rating in descending order. Then, it pairs the highest rated player with the lowest rated player, the second highest with the second lowest, and so on. It loops until all players are paired. If there is an odd number of players, the lowest rated player is dropped before pairing. The function returns a list of tuples, each containing two player names. For example, a list of four players pairs the best with the worst.

title: Server Request Load Balancer
spec: Write a function `dispatch(requests)` that takes a list of integer processing times representing incoming tasks. The function must assign these tasks to three identical servers to minimize the maximum load on any server. It initializes three integer variables to zero representing the current load of each server. It sorts the requests in descending order. Then, it iterates through the sorted requests, assigning each task to the server with the currently lowest total load. If there is a tie, it picks the first available server. The function returns a tuple of three integers representing the final total load on each server. For example, tasks of ten, five, and five will result in loads of ten, five, and five.

title: RPG Inventory Weight Manager
spec: Write a function `manage(items)` that takes a list of tuples, where each tuple contains an item name string, an integer weight, and a string category. The function must enforce a weight limit of one hundred. It loops through the items, keeping a running total of the weight. If adding an item exceeds the limit, it must discard items from the current inventory to make room. It prioritizes discarding items from the junk category first, then consumables. If it still cannot fit the new item, the new item is skipped. The function returns a list of names of the items successfully retained. For example, adding heavy items will cause junk items to be dropped.

title: Botanical Growth Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(conditions)` that takes a list of tuples representing daily weather, each containing a string weather type and an integer temperature. The function models the height of a plant starting at zero. It iterates through the days. If the weather is sunny and the temperature is between twenty and thirty, the plant grows two units. If it is rainy, it grows one unit regardless of temperature. If it is freezing, meaning temperature below zero, the plant shrinks by one unit, but its height cannot drop below zero. The function must track the height each day and return the final integer height. For example, three perfect sunny days will result in a height of six.

title: Dungeon Room Connectivity
spec: The function `explore(rooms)` receives a list of lists of integers representing paths between underground chambers. It must find the longest sequence of chambers that can be visited without repeating any chamber. The function should use a recursive search to evaluate all possible paths starting from chamber zero. If a chamber contains a negative integer, the path must immediately terminate. Return a tuple containing the maximum path length and the sum of all positive integers encountered on that longest path. For example, passing a list containing lists of connections should yield a tuple like four and fifteen.

title: Chip Inventory Allocator
spec: The function `allocate(requests, inventory)` receives a list of integer requested amounts and a list of integers representing the available counts of standard chip denominations: five hundred, one hundred, twenty five, five, and one. It must process each request in order and attempt to fulfill it using the largest chips possible from the available inventory. If a request can be fulfilled exactly, the inventory is permanently deducted, and the allocation is recorded. If a request cannot be fulfilled due to insufficient precise chips, it is skipped entirely without altering the inventory. The function returns a tuple containing a list of successful allocation tuples and a list of integers for the remaining inventory counts.

title: Message Cipher Shifter
spec: The function `shift(messages, offset)` receives a list of string messages and an integer offset. It must encrypt each message by shifting every alphabetic character forward in the alphabet by the given offset amount, wrapping around if necessary. Uppercase and lowercase letters must retain their original case. Furthermore, if a message contains any numeric digits, the entire shifted message must then be reversed. Any punctuation marks and spaces should be left completely unaltered during the shift, but will move position if the string is reversed. The function returns a list of the fully processed string messages.

title: Holiday Gift Assigner
spec: The function `assign(participants, exclusions)` receives a list of strings representing participant names and a list of tuples representing pairs of names that gave gifts to each other last year. It must pair each person with exactly one other person to give a gift to, ensuring nobody is assigned to themselves and no pair matches any of the given exclusions. The assignment should use a backtracking search to explore valid combinations in alphabetical order of the giver. If no valid assignment is possible, it must return an empty list. Otherwise, it should return a list of tuples where each tuple pairs a giver and a receiver.

title: Hardware Register Toggle
spec: The function `toggle(states, operations)` receives a list of boolean values representing the initial states of hardware relays and a list of integer indices. It must iterate through the operations and flip the boolean state of the relay at each specified index. However, if an operation targets an index that is currently true and its immediate neighbors are also true, the operation instead turns off the target and both neighbors. If an index is outside the bounds of the relay list, it should be ignored. After all operations, the function must count how many relays are in the true state. It returns a tuple containing the final list of boolean states and the integer count of active relays.

title: Mountain Valley Evaluator
spec: The function `evaluate(elevations)` receives a list of non negative integers representing a mountain terrain elevation profile. It must calculate the total volume of empty space that lies between the peaks, simulating where fog would settle. The logic should determine the highest elevation to the left and right of each position to find how much space exists above it. If the terrain is flat or strictly ascending, no fog is trapped. It should return an integer representing the total accumulated fog volume. Passing elevations zero, two, zero, three, one, two should return a volume of two.

title: Disk Block Defragmenter
spec: The function `defragment(blocks, locked)` receives a list of integers where positive numbers represent file identifiers and negative one represents empty space, along with a list of integer indices representing locked blocks. It must simulate a defragmentation process by moving all movable file blocks to the earliest available empty spaces in the list. Locked blocks cannot be moved, and empty spaces at locked indices cannot be overwritten. The function must iterate through the blocks and carefully swap movable files into valid empty slots while preserving their relative order. It returns the modified list of integers.

title: Machine Part Assembly
spec: The function `assemble(components)` receives a list of strings representing raw materials arriving on a conveyor belt. It must collect them into finished product sets, requiring exactly one metal casing, two screws, and one circuit board. If a defective component arrives, identified by a string starting with the word broken, the current partial set is entirely discarded and assembly restarts. The function must maintain running counts of valid materials and record a completed product when all required parts are present. It returns a tuple with the integer count of complete products and a list of strings for the leftover unused valid materials.

title: Stock Profit Maximizer
spec: The function `maximize(prices)` receives a list of floats representing the daily closing prices of a single stock over a period of time. It must determine the maximum profit achievable by executing at most two non overlapping transactions, where each transaction consists of a buy and a subsequent sell. The logic involves iterating through the prices to find the best split point that maximizes the sum of the profit before and after that day. If no profit can be made, it should return zero. Passing prices like three, three, five, zero, zero, three, one, four should return a profit of six.

title: Gene Sequence Aligner
spec: The function `align(sequences)` receives a list of string pairs representing short genetic sequences. For each pair, it must determine the longest common contiguous substring shared between the two strings. It iterates through all possible starting positions and lengths in the first string to check for matches in the second string. If multiple substrings tie for the longest length, the one that appears first in the first sequence is chosen. If there is no common substring at all, an empty string is recorded. The function returns a list of these longest common string matches.

title: Email Thread Reconstructor
spec: The function `thread(messages)` receives a list of tuples containing an integer message identifier, an integer parent identifier, and a string message body. A parent identifier of zero indicates a root message. The function must organize these messages into a nested hierarchy representing communication threads. It should process the list to match each reply to its parent, ignoring any messages whose parent identifiers do not correspond to any known message. The output must be a list of lists of integers, where each inner list represents a complete path of identifiers from a root message down to a leaf message. An input of three linked messages would yield a list containing a list of those three identifiers.

title: Machine Instruction Decoder
spec: The function `decode(instructions)` receives a list of strings representing binary machine code instructions, each exactly sixteen characters long. It must iterate through the list and translate each binary string into a tuple of an assembly operation name and an integer register number. The first four characters indicate the operation where zero is add, one is subtract, two is multiply, and three is divide. The remaining twelve characters are a binary integer representing the register. Any unknown operation code should produce an operation name of unknown. It returns a list of these tuples. An instruction starting with four zeros and ending with a one yields add and one.

title: Plumber Pipe Network
spec: The function `connect(pipes)` receives a list of tuples representing sections of pipe, where each tuple contains an integer start coordinate, an integer end coordinate, and a float representing the pressure capacity. The function must find continuous pipelines that start at coordinate zero and connect end to start without any gaps. It needs to calculate the maximum pressure each continuous pipeline can withstand, which is determined by the minimum capacity of its individual sections. Return a list of floats representing the maximum pressure for each valid continuous pipeline that reaches a coordinate greater than one hundred.

title: Broadcast Signal Overlap
spec: The function `detect(transmissions)` receives a list of tuples where each contains a string station identifier, an integer start frequency, an integer end frequency, and an integer power level. It must compare all pairs of stations to determine if any two stations have overlapping broadcasting bands. An overlap only causes interference if the difference in their power levels is less than ten units. The function should track all interfering pairs and compile a list of tuples containing the station identifiers, sorted alphabetically by the first identifier. Stations that overlap but have a large power difference operate safely and are ignored.

title: Memory Cache Eviction
spec: The function `evict(accesses, capacity)` receives a list of integer memory addresses and an integer capacity representing the maximum number of items a cache can hold. It must simulate a least recently used caching strategy. As the function iterates through the access sequence, it adds new addresses to the cache. If the cache is full when a new address is accessed, it must remove the address that was least recently used before adding the new one. The function tracks the total number of cache misses and returns this integer. Accessing three distinct addresses with a capacity of two will result in three misses.

title: Identification Code Validator
spec: The function `validate(codes)` takes a list of strings representing full identification numbers including a final verification digit. For each string, it must calculate the expected verification digit using a weighted sum. It multiplies the first digit by one, the second by two, and so on, summing these products. The sum is modulo divided by eleven, where a remainder of ten is represented by the character X. If the calculated character matches the final character of the string, the code is valid. If the string contains invalid characters or incorrect lengths, it is immediately invalid. The function returns a list of boolean values corresponding to the validity of each code.

title: Utility Bill Calculator
spec: The function `bill(readings)` receives a list of tuples, each containing a string customer identifier, an integer previous reading, and an integer current reading. It must calculate the usage by subtracting the previous reading from the current one. If the usage is negative, a rollover event occurred, and the usage is calculated assuming a maximum meter value of ten thousand. The bill uses tiered pricing: a base charge of fifteen, two per unit for the first hundred, three for the next two hundred, and five for any units beyond that. Customers with usage over five hundred are flagged. The function returns a tuple of a list of customer bills and a list of flagged customer identifiers.

title: Network Packet Fragmentation
spec: The function `fragment(payloads, size)` takes a list of string data payloads and an integer maximum payload size. It must split each payload into smaller chunks that strictly fit within the size limit. For each chunk, it must prepend a fixed length header consisting of a sequence number and the total number of chunks for that payload, formatted as integers separated by dashes. Additionally, if the original payload contains the word secret, the function must reverse each chunk before appending the header. It returns a list of all resulting formatted packet strings in order.

title: Seismic Fault Detector
spec: The function `monitor(measurements)` receives a list of integers representing consecutive readings from a seismic sensor. It must scan the sequence to identify significant events characterized by a rapid escalation in values. An event is defined as a sequence of at least three strictly increasing readings that culminates in a value at least one hundred units higher than the start of the sequence. Once an event is identified, the search resumes from the peak of that event. The function must gather the integer indices of the peaks of all valid events. It returns a list of these integer peak indices.

title: Assembly Batch Inspection
spec: The function `inspect(batches, threshold)` receives a list of lists of integers representing batches of manufactured parts with measurement tolerances, and an integer severity threshold. A part is defective if its absolute tolerance exceeds two. The function must scan each batch and classify it based on the defects. If a batch contains consecutive defective parts exceeding the severity threshold, it is marked as critical. If it just has more than three total defects, it is marked for review. The function returns a tuple containing the integer count of critical batches and a list of integer indices for the batches marked for review.

title: Flight Path Optimizer
spec: The function `optimize(waypoints)` receives a list of tuples containing integer horizontal and vertical coordinates representing a planned flight path. It must simplify the path by removing redundant waypoints that lie on the exact same straight line as their immediate neighbors. It evaluates groups of three consecutive points to check if their slopes are identical, indicating they are collinear. If they are, the middle point is discarded. This process is repeated until no more points can be removed. The function returns the simplified list of coordinate tuples. For points zero zero, one one, and two two, it returns zero zero and two two.

title: Cryptographic Block Verifier
spec: The function `verify(blocks, keys)` receives a list of string data blocks and a list of integer security keys. It must sequentially process each block to simulate a basic validation chain. For each block, it calculates a parity value by counting the number of vowels and multiplying by the corresponding security key. The validation rule requires that the calculated value of the current block plus the value of the previous block must be cleanly divisible by three. The first block is always assumed valid. If any block fails, the process stops. The function returns a tuple of the integer index of the first failure and the sum of all successful parity values.

title: Poetic Meter Analyzer
spec: The function `analyze(lines)` takes a list of strings representing lines of poetry. It must determine whether each line follows a strict alternating pattern of word lengths, switching between even and odd character counts. Punctuation should be stripped before counting the characters in a word. If a line is empty or consists of a single word, it is considered invalid. The function must evaluate all lines and compile the results. It returns a list of integer indices representing the lines that perfectly match this alternating word length pattern.

title: Satellite Coverage Calculator
spec: The function `calculate(coordinates)` receives a list of tuples representing satellite footprints, where each tuple contains an integer horizontal center, an integer vertical center, and an integer radius. It must determine how many discrete observation points fall within the coverage area of at least one satellite. The target region is a grid extending from zero to one hundred on both axes. The function iterates through all grid points and checks if the Euclidean distance to any satellite center is less than or equal to its radius. It returns an integer representing the total number of covered grid points.

title: Foreign Exchange Arbitrage
spec: The function `arbitrage(rates, amount)` receives a list of lists of floats representing a matrix of currency exchange rates between several currencies, and an integer starting amount in currency zero. It must explore all possible sequences of exactly three trades to determine the maximum possible return in currency zero. The rate matrix provides the multiplier for converting currency row to currency column. The function must simulate every valid path of three distinct conversions and track the resulting amounts. It returns a float representing the highest final amount achievable after exactly three trades.

title: Cron Schedule Expander
spec: Given a cron expression string with five fields separated by spaces representing minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week, and a tuple of five maximum limits, return a list of lists containing all valid values for each field. A field can be an asterisk meaning all values up to the limit, a single number, a comma separated list of numbers, or a hyphen separated range. Ensure parsed numbers are within zero and the corresponding limit. Example: `expand(cron, limits)` with asterisk one hyphen three, five, asterisk, asterisk and limits sixty, twenty four, thirty one, twelve, seven returns all sixty minutes, hours one two three, day five, all twelve months, and all seven days of the week.

title: Hospital Triage Simulator
spec: Process a list of patient records where each record is a tuple containing an arrival time, a severity from one to ten, and a treatment duration. The simulator maintains a waiting line and a single doctor who is available starting at time zero. When the doctor is free, the waiting patient with the highest severity is treated. If severities are tied, the one who arrived earlier is chosen. Return a list of tuples containing the patient original arrival time, severity, and the time their treatment is completed. Example: `triage(patients)` receiving a patient at time zero severity five duration ten and a patient at time two severity eight duration five. The higher severity goes next once the doctor finishes the first.

title: Shipping Box Formatter
spec: Distribute a list of item volumes into a list of available box capacities. The algorithm must sort the boxes from smallest to largest and the items from largest to smallest. It then attempts to place each item into the first box that currently has enough remaining capacity. If an item cannot fit into any existing box, it is left unpacked. Return a tuple containing the number of successfully packed items and a list of remaining capacities for each box in their sorted order. Example: `pack(items, boxes)` with items five and three and boxes four and six sorts boxes to four and six. Item five fits in box six leaving one. Item three fits in box four leaving one. Returns two items packed and remaining capacities one and one.

title: Overlapping Rectangle Area
spec: Calculate the total area covered by a list of rectangles on a two dimensional plane. Each rectangle is given as a tuple of four integers representing the left, bottom, right, and top coordinates. Since rectangles may overlap, simply summing the areas will overcount. Use a coordinate compression or grid based approach to calculate the exact union area. Return the total covered area as an integer. Example: `area(rectangles)` with two identical rectangles spanning from zero zero to ten ten will return a total area of one hundred, not two hundred.

title: Board Word Game Scorer
spec: Calculate the total points for a word placed on a game board. The input word is a string of uppercase letters. The multipliers input is a list of tuples corresponding to each letter in the word, where each tuple contains a letter multiplier and a word multiplier. The base value of letters follows standard rules where vowels are one point and harder letters like ze or ex are eight or ten points. First multiply each letter base value by its letter multiplier and sum these values. Then multiply the total sum by every word multiplier in the list. Example: `score(word, multipliers)` with a word cat where the first letter has a double letter multiplier and the last letter has a triple word multiplier.

title: Grid Ant Simulator
spec: Simulate the movement of an ant on an infinite grid of white and black squares for a given number of steps. The ant starts at coordinates zero zero facing north. All squares are initially white. In each step, if the ant is on a white square, it turns ninety degrees right, flips the color of the square to black, and moves forward one unit. If on a black square, it turns ninety degrees left, flips the color to white, and moves forward one unit. Return a tuple containing the final x and y coordinates of the ant and the total number of black squares on the grid. Example: `simulate(steps)` with one step returns coordinate one zero and one black square.

title: Color Palette Grouper
spec: Group a list of colors represented as tuples of red green and blue integer values. Two colors belong to the same group if the euclidean distance between their components is less than the given threshold. The grouping process should create a new group for the first color, then for each subsequent color check if it is within the threshold of the first color of any existing group. If it is, add it to that group, otherwise start a new group. Return a list of groups, where each group is a list of its color tuples. Example: `group(colors, threshold)` with pure red, pure blue, and off red will group pure red and off red together if the threshold is loose enough.

title: Wildcard String Matcher
spec: Implement a pattern matching algorithm that supports two special characters. A question mark matches any single character, and an asterisk matches any sequence of characters including the empty sequence. Both the pattern and the text consist of lowercase english letters and these special characters. Return a boolean indicating whether the entire text matches the pattern. The implementation should explore all possible matches for an asterisk, perhaps using a recursive approach or a two dimensional table. Example: `match(pattern, text)` with pattern a asterisk b question mark matching text a x y z b c returns true.

title: Timezone Meeting Scheduler
spec: Find available meeting times across two different time zones. The first input is a list of available hours for a local person, represented as integers from zero to twenty three. The second input is an integer representing the time zone offset of a remote person compared to the local person. The remote person is only available during their local business hours from nine to seventeen inclusive. Translate the local available hours to the remote time zone, check if they fall within the remote business hours, and return a list of the local hours that work for both parties. Example: `schedule(slots, offset)` with local availability nine and fourteen and offset plus five. Fourteen local is nineteen remote which is too late, so only nine works.

title: Robotic Arm Stacker
spec: Simulate a robotic arm moving blocks in a warehouse. There are five slots numbered zero to four. The arm can execute commands provided as a list of strings: left, right, grab, drop. The arm starts at slot zero and holds nothing. A grab command picks up a block from the current slot if it has one and the arm is empty. A drop command places a block in the current slot if the arm is holding one. Left and right commands move the arm, ignoring moves past the edges. All slots start with three blocks. Return a list of five integers representing the final number of blocks in each slot. Example: `stack(commands)` with grab, right, drop moves one block from the first slot to the second.

title: Plain Text Table Extractor
spec: Parse a list of string lines representing an ascii art table into a list of lists of strings. The table uses plus signs for corners, minus signs for horizontal borders, and vertical bars for column separators. Discard any line that starts with a plus sign. For the remaining lines, split the line by the vertical bar character, strip any leading or trailing whitespace from each cell, and discard empty strings resulting from the edges. Return the cleaned rows of data. Example: `extract(lines)` given a line with vertical bars bounding word one and word two yields a list containing word one and word two.

title: Cave Water Flow Simulator
spec: Simulate water filling a two dimensional cross section of a cave. The cave is provided as a list of strings where a hash denotes rock and a period denotes empty space. Water starts pouring into the top row at every empty space. In each step, water flows straight down if the space below is empty. If the space below is rock or already filled with water, it attempts to flow to the left and right simultaneously. Simulate this process until the water can no longer flow anywhere. Return the final state of the cave as a list of strings with water represented by the letter w. Example: `flow(cave)` with water dropping into a cup shape of rocks will fill the cup.

title: Income Tax Bracket Calculator
spec: Compute the total tax owed based on a progressive tax system. The income is an integer. The brackets input is a list of tuples where each tuple contains an income threshold and a tax rate percentage. The brackets are sorted by threshold. For each bracket, the tax applies only to the portion of income that exceeds its threshold but is below the threshold of the next bracket. Sum the tax amounts calculated for each applicable bracket segment. Return the total tax owed rounded down to the nearest integer. Example: `calculate(income, brackets)` with income one hundred and brackets zero at ten percent and fifty at twenty percent. First fifty is taxed at ten percent, next fifty at twenty percent.

title: Crossword Grid Generator
spec: Place a list of words into a blank twenty by twenty grid. The first word is placed horizontally in the center. For each subsequent word, search all previously placed words for a matching letter. If a match is found, attempt to place the new word perpendicular to the existing word such that they intersect at the matching letter. The placement must not cause the new word to go out of bounds or overwrite any non intersecting letters. If no valid placement is found, skip the word. Return a list of strings representing the final grid, using spaces for empty cells. Example: `generate(words)` with cat and apple could intersect at the letter a.

title: Roundabout Traffic Simulator
spec: Model the flow of cars through a simple single lane traffic circle with four entry points corresponding to north east south and west. The arrivals input is a list of tuples containing an entry point index from zero to three, a time of arrival, and an intended exit point index. A car will wait at its entry until the section of the roundabout immediately to its left is clear. Once entered, the car moves one section per time step until it reaches its exit. Return the maximum number of time steps any single car spent waiting to enter. Example: `simulate(arrivals)` with two cars arriving at the same time at adjacent entries will require one to yield.

title: Block Tower Stability Evaluator
spec: Determine if a tower of wooden blocks will stand or fall over. The tower is represented as a list of layers from bottom to top. Each layer is a list of three boolean values indicating whether a block is present in the left, middle, or right position. A layer is stable if its center of gravity is supported by the blocks in the layer immediately below it. Calculate the center of gravity for all blocks from the top down to any given level, and check if that point falls strictly within the outer bounds of the supporting blocks below. Return a boolean indicating if the entire tower is stable. Example: `evaluate(layers)` on a tower with only rightmost blocks on top of a single leftmost block will evaluate to false.

title: Sewing Pattern Stitcher
spec: Convert a sequence of stitch instructions into a visual representation on a ten by ten fabric grid. The pattern is a string of characters where u moves up, d moves down, l moves left, and r moves right. The needle starts at coordinates five five. Every time the needle moves, it leaves an asterisk character at both the starting and ending grid coordinates, and updates the current position. If a move goes outside the grid boundaries, ignore the move and stay in place. Return the fabric grid as a list of ten strings, where empty spaces are represented by periods. Example: `stitch(pattern)` moving up and right leaves asterisks along the path.

title: Number To Words Converter
spec: Translate a positive integer up to one billion into its english word equivalent. Break the number into chunks of three digits representing billions, millions, thousands, and ones. For each chunk, determine the words for the hundreds, tens, and units. Use standard english phrasing, such as twenty one, and append the appropriate scale word. Combine the chunks into a single space separated string, ignoring zero chunks. Return the final string. Example: `convert(number)` with one thousand two hundred thirty four becomes the words one thousand two hundred thirty four.

title: Auction Bidding Simulator
spec: Process a series of bids in a continuous auction. The input is a list of tuples where each tuple contains a bidder identifier, an arrival time, and their maximum willingness to pay. The auction maintains a current high bidder and a current asking price which starts at zero. When a new bid arrives, if their maximum exceeds the current asking price, the asking price increases to one dollar more than the previous maximum, and the new bidder becomes the highest. If two bidders tie, the earlier one wins. Return a tuple of the winning bidder identifier and the final price paid. Example: `auction(bids)` with bidder a at ten dollars and bidder b at fifteen dollars results in bidder b winning at eleven dollars.

title: Earthquake Magnitude Evaluator
spec: Analyze a list of integer sensor readings representing ground movement amplitude over time. Find the peak amplitude in the entire sequence. Then calculate the total energy by summing the squares of all readings that exceed ten percent of the peak amplitude. The magnitude is determined by taking the base ten logarithm of the total energy, multiplied by two, and rounded to one decimal place. If the list is empty or the peak is zero, return zero. Example: `evaluate(readings)` on a sequence of small numbers followed by a massive spike and small numbers will primarily use the spike and its immediate neighbors to compute the result.

title: Train Yard Shunter
spec: Organize train cars using a shunting yard with one incoming track, one outgoing track, and three holding sidings. The input is a list of train car numbers in random order. The goal is to move them to the outgoing track in ascending numerical order. You can move a car from the incoming track to any siding, or from a siding to the outgoing track. Always move the required next numerical car to the outgoing track if it is available at the end of any siding. Otherwise, place the incoming car onto the siding where the top car has the smallest value greater than the incoming car. Return a list of cars as they leave. Example: `shunt(trains)` receiving cars three, one, two sorts properly using the sidings.

title: Origami Fold Validator
spec: Verify a sequence of paper folding instructions to ensure they are physically possible on a square sheet initially spanning from zero to one hundred on both axes. Each fold is a tuple indicating an axis either horizontal or vertical, and a coordinate line to fold along. When a fold occurs, the paper on one side of the line reflects across to the other, shrinking the overall boundaries. If a fold line falls outside the current boundaries of the paper, it is invalid. Process the folds in order. Return true if all folds are valid, or false if any fold attempts to crease outside the paper edges. Example: `validate(folds)` checking a horizontal fold at fifty followed by another at twenty five returns true.

title: Vowel Shifting Cryptography
spec: Transform a given text message by shifting only its vowels while leaving consonants and punctuation in their original positions. Vowels are defined as a, e, i, o, and u in both uppercase and lowercase. Extract all vowels from the message in order, shift the entire sequence of vowels to the right by one position so the last vowel becomes the first, and then place them back into the message at the vowel positions. The case of the original vowel at that position must be preserved regardless of the shifted vowel. Return the transformed string. Example: `encrypt(message)` on the word hello becomes holle because the e and o swap, matching case.
